text: Was on a mission trying to find the perfect coat for the Holidays. Found my idea of the perfect coat at Burlington but they did not have my size. Went to Target, bought a coat but ended up taking it bath. Was not my dream coat. Next stop Ross. The only coat in my size was a beautiful Bomber style jacket made of pleather. Bought it right before Christmas. Now it's a few days after Christmas and my husband Guy points out to me that the coat is really wrinkled. I go on line and look up every possible hack to get wrinkles out of pleather. They all fail miserably. I just went back to Ross with that coat, no receipt, no tags and asked to speak to the manager. The manager is a young male with dark hair and black framed glasses. I tell him of my plight. He literally says go find what you need, no problem. WOW! You won't believe it, but there was my Camouflage coat, in my size, hanging there waiting for me. Oh the irony! They exchanged my coat and after all that I ended up with my Dream coat after all. Thank you Ross Dress for Less. You will forever be my first choice for now on!

I'm all about the bargains, but, can someone PLEASE clean the door handles???  I walked in at 10am this morning-the door handles on their double entrance doors and the door frame area around the handles were FILTHY!!!   I couldn't wait to clean my hands after being in this store-and it should NOT be that way.   No excuse, all the staff were standing around talking.    People, take some pride, huh, what about it???

I love shopping at Ross Stores. I stop at every one I come across. Yes, much of the merchandise is the same, but once in a while, you find a gem. It really is a treasure hunt.   They carry a selection of "as seen on Tv" stuff, a slew of Jr's clothing, a decent selection of ladies and missy, but they generally fail at plus, men's and petite.  These markets are woefully represented. Sure they have a men's section, but looking through the stuff, it's crappy t shirts and fubu jeans. Hardly anything the men in my life would wear.  This particular store's selection of lingerie/under garments is sad. They don't have a good variety of lingerie other than bras and panties.  Their home goods is very nicely situated as are their bed and bath items ... and their shoes!! My goodnes, their shoes are to die for!  One rhing I've noticed recently is that they are carrying many more high end designers: Michael Kors, Calvin Klein, and others at decent prices. So it does pay to shop at Ross.

Maybe my favorite location to visit at least once a week, especially when on this side of town. Their selection is random but unlike most other locations this one usually have items in my size especially shoes and sometimes hats but most of all its all about the "Selections" that draw me here. So I suggest you make a stop if you have the time.   One thing I learned about shopping at Ross, if you see something you like buy it. Don't wait, because it may not be there next time.

I love this store. I can find everything I need at this location!  Added 7/8/'17: My son lost over 50 pounds and we were able to outfield him with new clothes for his new figure for very little money. Yeah hey Ross‼

I have to agree with all the posts about the security at Ross (all Ross stores now).  It's one thing to have loss prevention staff to help your business save money, but over-aggressive, watch every move you make security staff are intrusive and rude.  I don't think I look like your typical shoplifter (maybe I do?? LOL), and the day I shopped for almost two hours I spent over $225.  I caught the security guy watching me several times.  It is creepy and makes someone want to go somewhere they can shop in peace.  I've worked retail.  I know you have to be aware of the shoppers, but come on, you're not a detective in hot pursuit of a hardened criminal.  At another Ross store, I (not willingly) overheard the security guard, a clerk, and what I think might have been a manager (!) flirting and talking about some really personal things LOUDLY.  Not cool.   And to Meg Z. (another Yelper who posted here), it most certainly is the clerk's job to remove the paper filling from a bag you purchase because she is supposed to be checking that no one put anything in there with intent to steal it.  You're right to be pissed about it because if the alarm had sounded at the door, you would have been blamed for sticking something in the purse you bought.

My two teenage girls love this store. I finally figured out why! You can buy a POS shirt and then just throw it away! They can wear a new shirt everyday! Considering they fall apart after one wearing or at least one washing. The few things I have bought for myself have gone to crap after two wearings and never quite get thier shape back after washing. It is a fun place to people watch though. I actually saw two older ladies fighting over a nightgown. Now you can't beat that!!  The staff is too rude for words. One commented on a tattoo I have and then had the nerve to ask me how much I paid. Shocked, I actually answered her. Then she proceeded to tell me that I paid too much for crappy work! WTF?? Will never go back!

This has to be the worst Ross I have ever been to.  It is a mess, everything is torn up...laying in isles, mismatched stuff on shelves.  Nothing makes sense in here it's organized like a landfill.  You can probably still find a deal in here, but it's gonna take all day wandering around.  Why do the "loss Prevention" guys wear a jacket marked loss prevention?? That seems pretty stupid.

Contrary to other reviews, this is NOT the worst Ross out there. Sure it has it's issues, and yes, like any other major discount retailers, the clothing is a bit jumbled and discombobulated. But for the most part it's an OK shopping experience.   The Loss Prevention person hangs out near the door, is more like a Walmart greeter, if you ask me. Yes, their presence is seen, but what do they actually do? Not a lot, really. Nothing they CAN do, honestly.  Since the holiday hours have been extended, they're currently open til 12:30 am or 1:30 am on any given night. This means, no long waiting lines to check out.   Heck! I walked away with 4 new dresses last night, all of them looked great.  I'll continue to shop here when I can!

Terrible worker lady running around putting clothes back on racks was extremely rude. Practically knocking into me as I was trying to look at items on a rack .  She never said excuse me or apologized.  Then she was banging on all the dressing room doors asking abruptly if everyone had a number for their items.  Seems they are in need of some customer service training.

I came in to try to exchange some slippers that I got for Christmas that were the wrong size. The selection of slippers was almost non existent! I really needed new slippers so I really did not look at anything else.   When I went to return them since they had been bought with a charge card I had to either take a store credit or put it on my card. I would have rather had cash but oh well.  The employees that I dealt with were nice and the store was clean. This store has always felt like a thrift store to me.

This Ross is located in a good location. Service is friendly, but lines are long at times. Not a huge selection of WOMANS clothing. I shop here only if I have an hour to browse. Usually I only leave with one item. Today I walked in and stood in return line. I had my daughter hold my spot. I was browsing the items they keep up front and was asked twice if I had a return. I said yes and they told me I needed to stand in the return line. I told them my daughter was holding my spot and I was browsing. They should consider moving this stuff back from the lines so people could look.

This place is alright, but given the closeout nature of the business, merchandise is never the same. Sometimes you'll find something great, and other times it will be complete junk. You have to shop carefully as not everything is a bargain. Decent prices all around though.   I would rate Ross higher, but the store always seems way understocked, and the cashier (cashiers if you are lucky) move as slow as molasses and never seem overly friendly (Ross doesn't pay too well from what I understand). It doesn't matter when you come, you will always be waiting in line at least 10 minutes. I always laugh that they have 6 or so registers but the most I have ever seen open is two.
Nothing special and not a large selection.  The creepy security guy at the door is a little scary but maybe he provides deterrence value.

I always shop at Ross Stores. The price is right and you can always find what you're looking for. However, one day I went in to purchase a new purse. At the cash wrap, I asked the cashier to remove the stuffing in the purse. She said, "Oh no, you can do that. That's not my job." What an asshole. Just that one comment is enough to make me never go back.

My husband and I go here quite often. Too often that even the security guards know us now. The selection is pretty good. If you just moved out and need kitchen tools, this is a great place to go for a fraction of the price you get in other stores.  The lines can get pretty long, so give yourself some time if you're going here.  Other than that, this place is pretty much self explanatory. Quality items for less

This Ross is in a convenient location close to many other stores and restaurants in Reno. Today I went in and noticed that maybe they recently re-stocked since there was a good variety in items. I bought three items and the associate that rang me up was having a side conversation with another associate. The focus she had on speaking with the other person unfortunately allowed her to open up the transaction with a greeting as well as asking if I had found everything I needed. I honestly am not one for small talk, so I didn't mind too much, however it's just one of those things you already expect as a courtesy. It wasn't until I got home and realized she failed to put one of the items I paid for in the bag. I called right away and another associate answered and took care of me over the phone. She also checked to see if I could go to another location closer to my home to get the item but they said no because it's a security measure. As nice as she was over the phone and let me know my item would be ready for me to pick up within 30 days there really was no accountability for the store or her co-workers' mistake.

Ross is amazing. This is the best Ross in Reno. It's clean. The sales associates are nice. This is the only place I can find clothing I like. They have other things besides women's clothing.  They hand clothes for all ages, Shoes, toys, kitchen gadgets, and more.... They have a return policy here to if that is something your in need of. I know some store do not have return policies.   They have dressing room to try clothing on!!! Alway a bonus. They are located right off the freeway which is convenient!  Their park lot space however are small. But I don't think they have much control over that.

There is very little merchandise to select from.  The wait for the sole cashier was very long.  I was jostled and pushed around on the line by a huge, inattentive mother with several unruly and spoiled kids...then when I asked the older female cashier why such a long wait, I was told no $ for payroll hence no workers.  wth,  give me break from this place.  Maybe there will be more stock and more than one cashier next time.  Wait it out to avoid,a headache..

I tend to find myself shopping at Ross weekly & always find (something ). Prices are great!  Store can be a little messy at times due to customers but their customer service & staff makes up for it! Surprisingly this location has long hours & is always busy. So if your in the area I do definitely recommend them. Why 4 stars & not 5? Well because they only have 1 restroom available towards the back of the store by the fitting room. 1 bathroom really? ! There's definitely room for improvement in the hardware of the shelf display- bathroom condition  (need baby station). Again it's Ross! Great deals - good & speedy - accurate checkout.
It's a typical Ross store, though a little smaller and not as much selection as other stores that I've been in.  The prices are about the same as other stores too.

Somehow, one of the items I was returning loss it's tag, and I must return it. A cashier that was very rude checked my receipt, and said it was not sold at the store. This was odd, as I bought this item with other clothing, which were validated. I was not expecting this much horrible service. Heck, I might not even go to this place again!

Beautiful selection of purses and shoes! Shoes in all sections were great and prices were indeed low. I think I found something I loved in every section in the store. Employees didn't seem to care too much on anything but getting out the store.. but that didn't help or harm my visit too much.

Horrible customer service... there's always 1 cashier and the manager talking on the phone! They need to get it together! There's nice things here but 10 customers in line and 1 person taking returns and purchases is very annoying.... Dondenna is the worst there besides being super slow!

I enjoy shopping at Ross because the prices are very good, but sometimes the selection is not the best. This time all thhe racks were full and they had a nice selection. Also you must come in often t see what they have, as it changes each week.  This Ross was very clean and the staff was friendly. I was greeted  by the cashier, who was helping someone, when i walked in. Also she said thanks for coming in when I left, even though I did not buy anything. Again she was with someone at her register.  The only thing that bothered my a bit, but I understand why, was when I was looking at wallets. The "Loss Prevention" guy was watching me very close. I know it could be easy to steel a wallet, but he could have been more discreet about whatching me.
Terrible dressing room scenario.  Too long a line and a wait.  Never coming back to this store!
I cashier in the entire store, nobody doing returns at 5:59 on a Friday evening. Unbelievable!! Talk about great service

This is an awful awful store. Normally, I would write out a long thoughtful review and attempt to highlight both the good and the bad. There is absolutely no point in doing that for this store. The store is dirty, customer service is horrible, and the items, what little they have, are nothing that you can not find at a better store.  Stay away from this store. There are far better shops you can spend your money at

Check this out -   Ross secretly has some cool stuff. Yes, I know it's depressing, and it looks like a gutted warehouse someone through racks of clothes in, and the shoes are also unorganized and some of their clothes looks like a granny, not an almost 24 yr old, would wear it.   All of that aside, I scored some SWEET dresses here for $13 each this past weekend. Don't brush them off. Check here first before dropping bigger bucks at those other stores.

I feel like Ross is a hit or miss store. Some Ross' I've been to have the chaos of a thrift store and others have the appeal of a department store. I think my reason, for shopping at Ross, is the same as everyone else's: the prices! You can get affordable, cute clothing, shoes and accessories for the home, at half the price of many places. I came here, most recently, in search of a dress. The store was clean and very well organized. Most sizes were all in their right locations. I found a ton of dresses, I loved, in just a matter of minutes and of course, I wanted to try them on! They have a ton of changing rooms, for both the men and women, which makes shopping all that much easier. They have a pretty large variety of stuff, in all their departments, but it is the luck of the find, as it is at many stores. Their children's section was wonderful! I found a bunch of Carter's stuff, at a third of the price it would be at a couple of the other stores I shop at, for kid's clothing. They had a clearance section with things marked down to just a couple dollars. Their home section is cute. I love their wall art. If you're looking to spice up a bland wall, for cheap, this is a great place to go! They had two cashiers working and even though there was a bit of a line, they busted everyone out in no time! The cashier, who rang me up, was polite and quick. The loss prevention guard, standing at the front door, seemed like he worked more as a greeter but he was kind and sociable as we were on our way in and out of the store. It turns out the dress, I purchased, had a tear in it and upon asking if I could return it, they were polite and helpful, as they answered my questions! I think this Ross store is very well-ran! I'll be back, that's for sure!

My cousin was in town for an event and needed a formal dress at the last minute.  I didn't expect to find anything in Ross, but they had what she needed, in the right color, for $30. I found a neat little painting for under $10.   In general Ross isn't the most organized store, but you can find great designer items at a really good price.  Come prepared for a scavenger hunt, but if you have the patience, it might be worthwhile.
Ridiculously loud music, extremely packed (do NOT go on a Sat), and filthy changing rooms. When I say filthy, I am not exaggerating. In addition to regular dust and dirt, I found specks of blood!!!

Unlike the branch on McCarran (see my other review) this RDFL actually has stuff to sell. It's your typical branch, with clothing, housewares, and other stuff, all at budget prices. I enjoy coming to RDFL for kitchen gadgets.   One thing that always amuses me: The conspicuous presence of "Loss Prevention" in the front of the store. They must have a serious theft problem...
Been in here lots of times and the customer service is seriously lacking most of the time... In fact they can be downright rude...
I've seen much nicer Ross' than this dump. Nothing is where it should be bad the cashiers are freaking rude!

Dress for less? Heck yes!  I really like Ross, and this location is no exception. The prices are fantastic! About a week ago I visited this store and found four (four!) dresses that I loved, each for $5 or $6. Seriously? That's just amazing. While Marshall's is very hit or miss, I always find something I like at Ross. And it's cheaper, too.  I came to this shopping center with a goal: to recreate an outfit I saw on Pinterest for (hopefully) cheaper than it would have been with the huge brands. I started at Kohl's (mistake) and was disappointed because nothing seemed even vaguely similar to what I was searching for and it was all so very expensive! I then walked down to Ross, and boy, was I pleased. I found two out of the three pieces I was looking for, for a grand total of twenty dollars. The time before that, I found a swimsuit for $2, and it was the cutest thing!  There is a great variety of brands here. I've seen Hollister, American Eagle, and many others all for a reduced price.  Listen, I love going to the mall and shopping there every now and then, but if you want to get more for your money, Ross is your best friend.
I hate shopping, but somehow I always end up watching my wife shop for stuff that is gonna break or doesn't fit.. thanks Ross!!!

Store was filthy dirty. Dust on all the purses and sunglasses. Nothing organized i.e. shoes scattered and not sorted by size, clothing not on correct size rack, dozens of panties on the ground under their rack, a large portion of the clothing hanging half off the hanger. Does anyone work here to put things away, sort or organize?  The dressing room was dirty and floors were gross. Plus the dressing attendant was just plain rude and unpleasant. I greeted her with a smile and a hello and she gave me a scowl, didn't utter any kind of response and wouldn't make eye contact. The gentleman at the cashier was very friendly and professional. I will not visit this location again.
This is the BEST Ross in Reno/Sparks.  Very clean and the associates are very helpful and nice.

Went there hoping to find a specific pair of shoes. The time was 11:40 and we read on google that it closed at 12. We walked in were told it was closing momentarily and I replied we'd be out before close. Went straight to the shoes and at 15 till close we're told on the intercom that we needed to put our stuff back or on layaway so we could pick it up the next day since registers were now closed. Really frustrating especially since half the lights were off. Is this typical?

I was in the area and wanted to see what they had for bath bombs, salts. I was highly disappointed to see a shelf and a half in disarray of random mismatched products. It looked more like a clearance rack, and most of the items they had were damaged.   The store was very crowded in the center isles and the perimeter was scare. I went to the pet section because I needed some things for the new puppy, luckily they kept up with this section and had a slightly better options than the bath.   I would not waste my time coming into this store, theres other options down the street from here.

This Ross is awful. It looks like it hasn't been restocked in months. Also the shoe department was very disappointing only containing little products that any kid would wear. I would give this store no stars if I was allowed. If I were to advise anyone, I would suggest going to a different Ross or stay away from this chain of clothing stores. Such a disappointment!!

This Ross store is really good.  The staff is very friendly...always a "hello" when you come through the door.  I have always found them helpful too.  I have gotten some really good clothing, and at such a good price.  Also, I just noticed today that they have gotten some good quality furniture and artwork in.    Thank you Ross!

My husband and I were able to find quite a lot of good deals here! My only complaint would be it seemed to be a little dirty. The employees acted like they wanted to chat with one another rather than provide good customer service. The lady that checked us out said one thing to us and that was saying she could help who was next and handed us our receipt and said the same thing to someone else rather than have a good day or such.

I'm fortunate enough to live near this location and it feels like "Home."  Often I need to shop late in the evening and being open til 10 is a life saver,  As I can not stand to be in a dressing room, I never try on clothes. I have never had an issue with returning a bad choice it outfit or just s poor choice.  I love the staff,.although sometimes there isn't enough I'm willing to.wait to get what I want at a reasonable price.

Every time I walk into Ross I check out the purse rack to see if they have the Calvin Klein purse I got in Hawaii for Artemis.. still holding strong.. have yet to see a duplicate :))) one of a kind xoxoxo just like my major steal today, Marc Jacobs outerwear!! Yayy! I love shopping!!!

Store has more security than cashiers. 30 plus ppl in line and only 2 cashiers working. What an earth you need security here?   I have to edit my review after finally paid at the cashier. She was so bored and her attitude was ridiculous. Absolute disgrace!! As I was in line I had the chance to watch how the employees were doing there job.  If I would be the owner, none of them would have been so lucky to stay here one more minute working or pretend to be working.  Ross! I would check twice who I hire.  Won't be back at this location for sure.  0 Star!

The ONLY reason I don't shop here more often is that I always find too much to buy. Sure, the store is in complete chaos, but you can't beat the prices for new clothing. Their selection is huge! Almost overwhelmingly so. I definitely appreciate finding Petite sizes here. Plus the departments & sections are well-labeled, as are the individual hangers, so browsing is easy. Surprisingly, with all the mayhem of customers here, I don't usually notice too many articles misplaced.  The fitting room is gigantic! Tiny stalls, but LOTS of them. However, there's usually only one attendant, counting items, so typically there's a bit of a wait. Also, the checkout area can be tedious. But, the line moves quickly.   Don't forget Ross carries items for your home at great prices, too. Other locations may be larger & less cluttered, but this one packs a lot into the space, and it's not far from my house.

Good grief Ross just totally sucks. Their selection is awful. What has happened to this chain in the past 5-yrs?!? It just gets worse every year. The clothing is just terrible. It's seriously all the reject clothes from a Goodwill or close to it. I'm done shopping at Ross. This Ross is no different - always bad selection, a complete dirty mess and I get sick of the high level (ha ha) security always making customers feel like they've stolen something before you even get thru the front door. Major thumbs down. Would not be shocked to see Ross hit BK in the next 2-3 years. Oh and their return line is a joke - always a big major deal to return something. God forbid the tag not match the actual description in their computer! Cuz if it don't they make you feel like you switched something out to return instead. Ain't a customers fault if a attached tag doesent match your computers description. Don't assume the worst with customers and give the benefit of the doubt.

I love it, I got it at Ross. Really. I hit Ross up today to look for some less than really expensive dresses and walked away spending over a Benjamin on two new dresses, two shirts, a straightening iron, satin sheets and a satin comforter and a martini shaker.  The place was very clean and organized. The woman working in the fitting room was a delight, very helpful and very sweetly complimented my selections. The fella at the checkout counter was a doll, too.

Ross is a last resort when it comes to shopping for pretty much anything. This particular location is maybe my least favorite, due to the fact that there's always only one register open and it's usually a senior citizen with no urgency or personality. Today was no exception-one register open, old lady running it and a line forming, apparently in the wrong place because when another employee came up to relieve the line-looking disgruntled because she stopped what she was doing to do so-yells out, "THE LINE STARTS HERE, NOT THERE!" Needless to say, I shan't be returning.

Always disorganized lol- I can't help but feel the chaos, as I saw Ross employees constantly following customers to try and catch shop lifters- what's the point of having  Loss Prevention staff at the door- if everyone is going to be followed around like a criminals?

If we didn't have to rate it with stars I wouldn't. This Ross location does not deserve a rating. It has been the nastiest Ross store  for years. It seems like this is the location that all the other Ross stores send their unwanted clothes to.  It is nasty inside, (nasty as in a hurricane hit it) unorganized, overpacked with too much, things flow in to the floor, no one literally no one speaks English. The music is loud the customers are louder. You can tell that the employees are not happy working there. But like I said this is been going on for years apparently Ross doesn't care to fix the issue.  they just need an true overhaul
Big store, lots of clothing.  Not alot of dresses (especially holiday) to choose from.  They did have lots of clearance sales.  Had some cute dog clothes which were on the pricey side.

This store constantly looks disarrayed, and don't even think about using their public bathrooms. There is a noticeable urine smell when entering in the hallway leading to the bathrooms. Which should be a huge indicator not to use their bathrooms by any means- There is about a foot of black tar dirt stains that are on the floors from all four corners of the bathroom walls. There are some good finds, if you can overlook the dirtiness of this facility. If only they cleaned with proper cleaning products, the offensive urine smell would disappear.

It may not look pretty, but it definitely gets the job done. Many a time would there be when i run in there right before the gym because i need something (ie ear buds, headphones, and most recently, shoes to exercise in because the ones i had on worn down completely on the heel) and you actually find really good deals on otherwise expensive items. Two things I've gotten here were a pair of Philips headphones that are super comfy, still in good condition, and still work. My most recent buy was a pair of knockoff (or so i assume) Skechers that i spotted and fit great. Sometimes i'll feel like browsing a little, and they actually have a decent selection of shoes, bags, and dresses. Great place to go too during the holidays for rare, gourmet, and discounted finds. Next time I need athletic gear, I'll be sure to check with them first to avoid spending a fortune. Chances are, i might walk off with a little more than what i was looking for.
New layout is awful I won't be back, skip this location for the citrus Park where you can shop and check out

Depressing comes to mind.   The lighting is dull and so is the supply and choice one finds here. Empty shelves and those with product are sparse at best. It reminds me of a very bad thrift store that is about to go out of business.   Freakin weird I tells ya.

Update:  This Ross is getting worse and worse !!!! I mean the staff is ridiculously rude and only 1 person working again! 10 people in line..... I had charlita today oh god talk about bad service!     Horrible customer service... there's always 1 cashier and the manager talking on the phone! They need to get it together! There's nice things here but 10 customers in line and 1 person taking returns and purchases is very annoying.... Dondenna is the worst there besides being super slow!

Needed a box and colored pens and found them here.   Is the store in somewhat of a disarray? Yes. Is there a security guard standing at the front to stop people from stealing? Yes. Does the cashier look like she hates her life? Yes. But I found exactly what I was looking for, so that gets an A-OK from me.  We started at the Dollar Tree looking for a cute box and colored pens and struck out. I really didn't want to pack a car hating child to go to Target when I still had to go to PDQ and they were in opposite directions, so I decided to try my luck at Ross.  I know, most people shop at Ross for clothes, but their home goods section is rapidly expanding and they have great options. I found an awesome box and colored pens - neither were cheap looking, but they were cheap! Total win.   I got to see the security guard in action when the cashier thought a family was trying to steal something. It was a miscommunication, but I've never seen a loss prevention officer before. It made me a little sad that they don't trust their patrons, but I'm sure they also have good reason. The cashier was actually super nice to my son, so there's that.   We were in and out relatively quickly. Both the workers and patrons were friendly (they let me cut in line when they saw my son starting to flail). I will definitely come back to this Ross when I'm looking for something random.

Caveat Emptor (BUYER BEWARE). If you shop at Ross be cognizant of how you pay for your purchase if you pay for part of your purchase with a gift card/merchandise credit. Their return policy is set up to keep your $ The cashier scans your merchandise then gives you the total cost due. You have a merchandise credit so you give that to the cashier. She deducts that amount from the total and gives you the balance due. You pay the balance in real cash money. E.g., Your total due was $88.74. You want to apply the merchandise credit that you have. The credit is for $$18.42 so you hand this to the cashier and wait for the balance due. The balance due is $70.33. You pay this amount in cash. Now, you have a return in the amount of $7.99 plus sales tax ($8.55). They tell you you that they have to give you a merchandise credit (not because you're beyond the date of return), but because you used the merchandise credit as your first form of payment. Why should they be able to deny you cash back for an $8 item when you've given them over $70 in cash. NEVER, NEVER pay with a merchandise credit first if you think you might have a return  They will force you to take a merchandise credit and will not refund any cash.... simply because you used the merchandise credit as your first form of payment. You should be able to get your cash back to the amount you paid....then a merchandise credit. Hypothetically, say I have another return the next day totaling $25 are they again going to force me to take another merchandise credit because it was my first form of payment even though the initial merchandise credit was for less ($18.41)? Now, add $25 and $8.55 for a total of $33.55. Now, you are forced to take the $25 return and the $8.55 as a merchandise credit totaling $33.55 when the initial credit was only $18.41. They are denying you any cash back and forcing you to keep your $ in their store. You should be able to get your cash back to the amount in which you paid then the balance issued in a store credit. Lesson....if you have a merchandise credit use it as your last form of payment, not your first. Once you have your total amount due....do the math. Subtract the merchandise credit amount from the total and pay that amount in the payment of your choosing ( cash, credit, debit) then pay the balance lastly with the merchandise credit. This may hold up the line while you do your calculating and the cashier won't like it, but it's your hard earned cash we're talking about. Their policy does not have your best interest at heart. You have to be smart and play their game. Especially now, with Covid and dressing rooms are closed you're likely to have returns. I've done my best to try to explain how they are keeping your money. Remember, first form of payment should be anything except the merchandise credit.....use the credit as your last form of payment. Another sneaky thing they do to keep your money has to do with a return/purchase. If you have a return and are going to make another purchase typically, they will ask you if you just want them to apply that return to your new purchase. To keep things simple you will probably agree to that. If you do agree to that and you have a return they are going to give you that return as a merchandise credit because you used that as your form of payment..... even if you paid cash for the merchandise being returned. Actually, if the the security guard at the front door sees you come in with the return they tell you to go ahead and go in and shop first and then do your return at the same time so you don't have to stand in line twice. Really, it's just another way for them to make that exchange and then keep your money if you have a return and give it back to you in a merchandise credit. I view their return policy as a license to steal from me. If I've paid $70 in cash and $18 in store credit and return an $8 item I should be able to get my cash back up to the $70, which I paid then anything over that should go to the merchandise credit. For me, it's not about the $8, it's about principle. The customer service is horrible. I have especially had issues at the Countryside/Clearwater location.

Be careful working here!! Person training me asked me to take cash out and leave it in her locker and poor me listening and trusting I end up with the blame! Sick world! Glad I can share this some way now! Please new people be careful!! If I can only explain the fear and traumatizing situation I went through!!

I've been to this location multi times now- & during the era of Covid -19... I must say I'm very impressed. Racks are spaced out, social Distancing is actively encouraged to employees & masks are provided to anyone without one. Hand sanitizer is also available at multi convenient locations- as well as masks are avail for sale for adults & children at the front of the store. This is one of the few places I've felt ok shopping at- as a high risk person. So whether u need slippers a pan or a pillow- let alone a pullover- come shop at this store doing it right!

I have to give this experience 3 stars, and I'll tell you why. It was a Thursday afternoon and all they had was 1 cashier. The line kept getting longer and longer. She called for assistance at the checkout counter at least 2 times while I was in line. I felt really bad for her because she was doing a great job trying to move the line along. She did the best that she could under the circumstances. The management at this store need to come out and assist if no one else is available. There was an employee stocking the area where you form the line with useless crap while all of us were waiting. Maybe he's not trained in checking people out. Train him! It was ridiculous!  Other than that, the store is one of the newer ones in the area. It still remains neat and organized unlike the one near the mall. I'd go back to browse but I'm not sure if I want to wait in that line again. Some people walked out. No bueno.

This ROSS is in a great location. The prices are inexpensive. I did notice Shoppers leaving their children running around the store screaming and unattended. Employees are not your babysitters! Also I have seen rude customers actually throw merchandise on the floor or curse out the employees for no reason other than some customers are RUDE, DISRESPECTFUL, RACIST TOWARDS EMPLOYEES WHO ARE WORKING HARD HOWEVER, THEY HAVE AN ACCENT??? WHAT IS WRONG WITH THESE CUSTOMERS MANY WHOM ARE FOREIGNERS THEMSELVES!! UNBELIVABLE! I would never allow any customer to treat me with disdain or hatred as I'm doing my job, following the policies of ROSS DRESS FOR LESS. Go to Macy's, Nordstrom's and ACT OUT LIKE YOU DO AT ROSS, THEY ASK YOU TO LEAVE OR THROW YOU OUT! Please if you don't have class and some sort of grace, please do me a favor as a frequent CUSTOMER.....SHOP SOMEWHERE ELSE WITH YOUR RACISTS ATTITUDE! Evelyn D. Waters

Normally I like this store (well, their other locations). The selection at this location is quite sparse. A lot of their shelves and racks are empty or just have a few things on them. Last time I was there, the associates in the store were a bit rude to one of the customers when I was up at the register. I recommend this store, but not this location.

No words, just no words. There are people who love this type of stores, this is not me! I am not sure why I am being dragged to one of those every weekend. I guess I need to re-evaluate my life choices.   But if you want the last year's fashion in a moderate price. Go here!

Ross Dress for Less should be renamed... Ross unkind to disabled people... their carts cannot be wheeled to ones car.  No bueno ...  I need to lean on the cart to get to my car if my cart is full of semi-heavy items.  They said if I drive my car up to the curb in front of the door, someone will bring my things out.  So this disabled person is supposed to deal with extra traffic and pedestrians, eventually getting to the front of their shop, only to get back out of my car to open the back up for the person to put my stuff in for me.  I don't think Ross management thought this through with an understanding of so many situations a disabled person might have to face.  Maybe I'll change it to 1 star... yeah, on second thought, they just lost another star..
About 5 people In line and about 8-9 employees just standing around doing nothing. 1 person on register. Left my cart right there and walked out
This is a bare-bone Ross store and it is a hit or miss.  I go frequently looking for things but usually leave empty handed because the selection is minimal.

What is the point of a HOLD ticket if associates are going to allow other customers to take items off?!? Came during my lunch break and had to put dresses on hold for when I got off work. When I returned several items were missing. Extremely disappointed.
I went in for men's khakis.  No selection at all.  The bathroom was obviously not cleaned in a while.
Who knew the kind of buys you can get a Ross.   Clark shoes for under $40.   Cute jeans.   Lots of gift ideas either clothes, kitchen items even some furniture.

After eating breakfast in the area, I popped into this location and wasn't overly impressed.  I tend to check out the men's clothing when I head into a closeout store because you never know what you may find. Their selection was extremely limited and nothing seemed to catch my eye.   I will say the store was very neat and organized compared to most Ross locations. Maybe that's because they didn't have a ton of product, but at least it was clean. Maybe I caught them at a bad time, but I didn't see anything that would bring me back to this specific location.  Obviously, different locations have to cater to their geographical crowd and this location didn't carry the brands of clothing that I am used to wearing.

This Ross store moved, with great fanfare, from one side of McCarran to the other. So itrequired a visit to see what the new place looks like. Disappointment disappointment because it might be one of the worst Ross stores I've ever seen. Everything is in a state of disarray. The lack of merchandise and the lack of organization and the lackadaisical attitude of store personnel sent me to the exits pretty quickly.
The WORST custmer service ever in department store...!!!!!! I don't even understand why the managers hired these people...!!!!!!! I only have bad memories from here...

This place is beyond disrespectful! I PLEDGE TO NEVER RETURN TO THIS STORE EVER EVER EVER AGAIN! The fitting room is absolutely garbage just like the rude employees! Out of all the times I went there that I could possibly remember, I've never seen anything like this before. Today, Was a very uncalled for rudely treated visit at Ross. The fitting room lady that's so called "in charge" was ABSOLUTELY OUTRAGES AND VERYYY RUDE AND UNCALLED FOR!  My mom asked the rude wannabe bad a**  if I could fit in. She says, "excuse me in a bad rude way!" She starts getting an attitude my friend obviously defended herself. She kept saying bye bye ok. And, MORE DISRESPECTFUL THINGS THAT MADE ME WANT TO THROUGH THE CLOTHES  IN HER #&*## FACE! (Not to offend anyone but the truth on how they act) They act ghetto towards a lot of people out of my own experience and the reviews on how people act. There are multiple reviews of them being rude to people over the fitting rooms.

I've been to Ross in South Jersey and in New Castle, DE but this was my first time at this one in Center City Philly. It's big inside considering the fact that it's in a mall under construction but they have a lot. I'm pretty sure that got sales going on all the time.

I like that I can walk into this store and leave with a lot of stuff paying little money... BUT you spend a long time in there because it's disorganized, the dressing room seems like its from a slasher movie, and a lot of the staff members are pretty rude (on my most recent visit the dressing room attendant made everyone put their the clothes away as her and her 2 co-workers were just standing around gossiping... no wonder its disorganized... but i digress)...    and don't forget to check out th e homeware section across the hallway... great for new apartments

I'm completely in shock by what I saw when I walked into this Ross. It was a befuddled mess in here! Before I even walked inside I could see the checkout line stretched all the way down the aisle. I've been to Ross before when I lived in Texas and it was a great place to shop. This is nothing like that store! Clothes were everywhere and not even in the right order or size, shoes mismatched and looked like they were already worn...it was bad. Even the patrons inside looked like they could've been featured on the People of Walmart site. I won't be coming back to this location. I'm hoping the Ross in Franklin is much better. Not all Ross stores are created equal.

This ross makes me giggle to walk through. They have a varied selections, and a varied clientele and staff. It's a great hodgepodge of different fun to be had. Depending on the day you might find a great deal on some boots, dresses, or anything really. Or you might see a young couple having a grueling fight, or teenagers stealing things. It's really a plethora of different delights.   Basically I just shop there, but the people watching can be very epic as well. Going right after work or during lunch can be seriously intense because the lines get out of control, but you'll probably find something to make it worth your stay.

January in Philly and nary a pair of gloves or hat in sight!! What the front door??!  BUT the staff were SO nice about the whole thing that I actually didnt mind turning around & walking back out into the frigid cold

I've been to this Ross about twice now. First time, I needed some socks so it was in and out but I still noticed that the employees aren't cheery or friendly. They just check you out. Second time, I went to look for a few tops. I noticed that the selection was skimpy and it wasn't very organized nor clean. The store ran out of Ross bags and they resorted to clear trash lining bags. I've been to a number of Ross and this has to be one of the worst ones.

The only reason to venture to this gross place is the awesome deals. I LOVE Ross stores and whenever I can't get to one in the suburbs I have to gather all of my strength and patience to go to this one.  There are tons of great deals from dresses, to shoes, to house stuff, and I always find something for the closet or the house...but the atmosphere...is not pleasant.  People that work there are extremely unprofessional, last time I was there they were literally standing by the register discussing in detail their weekends ignoring the long line. One girl was just brushing her hair like it was her house? Everyone looks miserable and unhappy to be there. The dressing rooms are disgusting, with the weirdest bathroom smell and most of them don't close. There are always tons of loud and obnoxious people there...with kids. And the line is always long and slow moving.  So yes, I love Ross but I hate this store...so good luck! =(

I love Ross! The bargains can be incredible and they always are getting new stuff in so you've gotta be quick and impulse buy. The staff are pretty nice too. I must go in there a lot because the security guards recognize me. The one complaint is that the register lines are slow but you've just gotta be prepared for that and not be in a hurry. It's like Aldi, where t's worth not having as many staff and waiting a bit longer to keep the prices lower.
Meh. Is all I really have to say. It was a total disappointment. The only reason I gave 2 stars was because my mum found one shirt she liked.

Not sure why there are poor reviews for this place? But you get exactly what you should expect. It is after all a discount clothing store. If you have some patience you can find some great deals of some real good clothing. With that said, it is going to be a bit of a mess in there, so be prepared but who goes clothes shopping for anything other than getting new sparkly clothes so you can go run the town.  Its not a bad place, I am not too snooty to shop here either, maybe the others feel they are too good to shop in a place like this? Who knows, but when I am after a decent pair of jeans for a decent price this is a good place to start.

I'll preface this review by saying I love to 'treasure hunt' at places like Ross, TJ Maxx and (maybe someday in Nashville - PLEASE!!!) my favorite; Nordstrom Rack. I grew up trying to find cheap 'trends' for back to school at these places, as my parents gave us $200 and we had to make due.   That being said, this is the worst Ross ever, which is mighty mighty unfortunate as its 2 seconds from my house and in any other case I'd be there regularly. Its always been dingy and had long lines, but lately its included the following:  Zero selection: it looks like its going out of business but its not. I can always count on a cute dress here, but lately its been mumu's rejected from my old Girl Scout leader and a pant suit my granny would eschew from her 'church line'. Additionally the entire wall that used to be full of useful small items like running socks, hair bands and panty hose is literally barren.  Customer Service: Um, there is none. I recently returned a dress on the 30th day (I know, my bad) and still received a flimsy paper voucher for my 'credit' - they cant even offer a gift card. Like I'm not going to lose a 1 x 2 inch piece of paper? I also waited in line for 25 minutes while some guy sat behind the desk right in front of me filling out paper work (he was a manager). Priorities much?  Blech, the aisles are always awkward, the sizes never in order and the 'loss prevention staff' are obvious and super creepy.   Look, I'm obviously not in Nordy's and don't expect as much, but this place has gotten so low brow and ridiculous I will save my bargain finding fun during trips to Portland/Atlanta for H & M and the Rack.

Ross!  I went into the store today to check on your progress since my last review!  I was shocked to discover that you have actually learned something!  I walked in, and I immediately noticed that the clothing was more organized on the racks, there were no messes or clothes on the floor and things were grouped together by size!  The second thing I noticed was 4 (count 'em) FOUR registers were open, as opposed to the previous count of one total open register!  There was still a line, but it moved quickly and there wasn't a long wait to check out.  It was fantastic!  I rewarded your efforts today, by not only purchasing a dress (I was able to find it easily, because the racks were organized by size and the fast moving line gave me no excuse to not get it), but by coming on here and boosting you up a star.  Why not a boost of 2 stars?  I want to make sure that this isn't a fluke, Ross.  Don't get lazy as the summer goes on.  Keep up the good work and that fourth star will be yours, and I will visit your place more often.

They have  really amazing stuff , and I love shopping there. But every time I am there, the customer service is worse and worse.  My last experience, I picked up these shorts that didn't have a price tag and instead of asking for a price check she just randomly named a price. When she was scanning my items she was literally just banging things like hangers on the table. She looked super pissed. When i asked her to get some help from someone for price check she said there's no one here. Really ??? Because earlier when I was trying on my clothes, I had to wait till the three ladies at the fitting room finished their discussion about clothes, lunch and haircuts. I started talking to my husband to kill time and one of the ladies gives me this attitude saying "do u wanna try these on or not ? I am trying to talk to you" really ? How would I know ?  Terrible experience like always. If they didn't have reasonably priced stuff, I would never return.  You can go here to shop, but don't expect any pleasant experience. They really need to work on their customer service skills.

Oh, Ross, you are an enigma wrapped in a riddle wrapped in a mess.  Let's start with the good.  You carry all kind of clothes, but specifically, the dresses you carry are great.  I can find anything here, from casual to dressy and for a really great price.  There are dresses here from the same brand as dresses I have seen at Dillard's (for a lot more money).  I love to come here and look for a nice sundress, when I need one for a summer party and the ones I have have become boring.  Now, the bad.  Oh, Ross.  Why do you have only one register open out of seven?  Don't you see the super long line this creates?  Don't you realize that most times I don't visit you, because the length of time I stand in line isn't worth the money I will be saving by patronizing you?  I mean, there are TWO greeters at the door.  Couldn't one of those ladies be working another register?  Certainly they have more skill than just saying, "Welcome to Ross!" when I walk in.   Also, your aisles are super narrow and your shopping carts are super wide.  I understand that you are pressed for space, but a few inches would make a world of difference.  Also, wouldn't it make sense for customers to NOT push their wide carts down the aisles, thus blocking anyone else who would like to shop in said aisle, but can't, because it would be a squeeze?  I thought this was common sense, but here we are.   Last but not least, all of the sizes are mixed up.  You have 2's mingling with 12's and 6's cavorting with 10's.  There's no rhyme or reason to this.  That's one thing if I'm at a thrift store, but Ross, you aren't a thrift store.  Don't sell yourself short.  Get organized!  Let's be honest, Ross, I am being very generous with my two stars.  You know it.  I know it.  So many simple changes could be made in order to make this store great.  PLEASE start with opening more registers.  There are people who would LOVE a job right now.  Hire more people.    In conclusion, Ross, you have an assignment: 1) Hire more people and open more registers. 2) Expand the aisles.  More space means more shoppers! 3) Organize your selections by size!  2,4,6,8,10,12...etc.  In that order, Ross!  Don't get creative!

This Ross store has a special place in my heart.  It is sort of the drunk and disorderly little sister of the deep-discount box stores, but oh, the treasures that await!  Maybe in part because of the disorganization, I have had great luck finding off-season stuff...  flower pots in the winter, gloves in the summer, random things that you wouldn't find at other stores.  I had great luck recently with curtain rods, but I did have to bring back one of the first ones because I managed to buy one which, despite being in the box, was missing half of the rod.  It is really great but really exhausting to go to this store - I can understand why some would stick with Marshalls or Stein Mart.  At the same time, if you are not hungry, cranky, or wearing uncomfortable shoes, I would recommend giving this store a try because you can really find some great bargains!  And if all else fails, you can walk next door to Target and regain your composure in a clean, orderly retail atmosphere.

Ross - Dress for Less!    Das ist der Inbegriff für Schnäppchenjäger auf amerikanischen Boden. So gut wie in jeder größeren Stadt gibt es die grossen Ross Märkte.    Ross ist mehr oder weniger ein Outletstore für Damen-, Kinder- und Herrenbekleidung.    Die Kette kauft Restbestände von Markenartikeln in großen Mengen ein. Diese werden auf meterlangen Stangen nach Größen und Art der Ware geordnet. So hat man schon mal ein Stange von 10 Metern nur mit Poloshirts in Größe Large.    Hier braucht man Zeit und einen gewissen Suchsinn. Wenn man dann aber etwas gefunden hat, bekommt die Markenartikel für wenig Geld.

Found good deals and fast check out! My wife is 6 months pregnant and was looking for cute maternity shorts and founds some great ones she truly loved. We didnt think we would actually find maternity clothes but they have a nice selection.

Ross... first off, I forgot this store is broken up into 2 parts. If you're a guy and you're shopping for yourself don't even bother with the 8th and Market St. entrance. Just make a left and enter at the middle of the block and then left again for the men's... Ross.  This review is for the fragrance section. I've heard some great things... that great scents could be found here, but it's very much hit or miss and much of that could be based on location. I could imagine that this is the type of place where a stock person could hide the best offerings to buy for themselves. Anyway, there's definitely some truth to what I heard. I went to the mall (King of Prussia) after leaving here and I found some of the very same scents at Lord and Taylor and Macy's at twice the price (D&G, Burberry, Ralph Lauren, to name a few). While they're at the lower end of the spectrum for department stores they have stronger selections than what you'd find here in Philly.  So there are 2 reasons why you should be checking out Ross now and then.   1. You never know what you might find.  2. You never know where it might come from.  A major part of catching these deals is being there at the right time and knowing what to look for (because there will be no sampling... correct me if I'm wrong). The selection definitely looks picked over or disheveled, but the scents themselves are boxed in plastic and I think some even had an extra theft proof box around them.  I'll be back.  FUN-FACT: The women's scents are on the women's side... Oh snaps!

I can't believe I've yet to write a review for Ross. This has been one of my favorite stores since I first found it in San Francisco in 2002. I was thrilled to spot one here on Market Street when I moved to Philly, too!!   This store is a great place to find brand-name clothing that's in good condition - that just didn't sell at other retail stores for one reason or another. I've found great deals, on very cute clothes, shoes, and accessories each time I've shopped at a Ross.  NOTE: It does take some scrounging and some time to comb through each of the overly-stocked racks - so don't just come in to browse for a few minutes. This is serious shopping. This place is all about the "diamond-in-the-rough"s.

Sunday afternoon- ALL 3 checkout girls were clearly unhappy, the line was consistently very long and the fitting room lady looked overworked and very frustrated. This store has changed, Hermitage has changed and needs a lot of attention. I don't plan to visit Ross in Hermitage anytime soon.

While I would like to have a look at what they have (I'm assuming it's like TJ Maxx or marshall's), I just can not stand the crowded, disorganized atmosphere. Everything is out of place. Size 6 is NOT the same as size 9 in shoes.  Kids run rampant. The line for the sole cashier was across the store all the way to the wall.  I felt like I needed a Xanax to even be in there. I couldn't get out fast enough.  I'm giving it one star because I think there might be some good deals there. Somewhere.

Dress for less, ein absolutes "Must go" wenn man in den USA ist.  Man bekommt Waren von letzten saison oder reststände von Markenbekleidung.  Preise bis zu 80 % reduziert vom original Preis.  Damen und Herrenbekleidung sowie für Kinder. Von Unterwäsche bis zum Anzug alles dabei, sowie Sport und Outdoorbekleudung.  Ich war teilweise in einem gewissen rytmus drin da wöchentlich neue waren kommen, die natürlich aufgrund der Preise auch schnell vergriffen sind!    Man bekommt auch haushaltswaren, Bettwäsche und Koffer günstig!    Bringen sie viel Zeit mit, da das shoppingherz aufgeht und beim stöbern viel Zeit vergeht! :-)

the store is divided into two separate buildings ,not a problem. great place to find something ,but not enough cashiers. could use more big men and plus woman clothing variety. staff rude to not too rude ,but you get what you pay for.

I only went here once but there was so much clothes in my size and I found so many cool things!! Hello, can you come to my location. My Ross sucks here!! Thanks! I'm gonna have to fly back to this Ross. LOL

I LOVE Ross!!! I bought an awesome Columbia sport shirt at this store for only $12!! The only annoying thing was the fitting room, loud women screaming at one another, they were so loud you could hear them in the store. I think the employees could have said something. Oh well, guess you don't shop at Ross for the nice surrounding but instead the bargains.

Messy, disorganized, kind of my personal nightmare. I'm not usually much of a Ross shopper anyway (to be upfront about it), because the thought of 100 different dresses on one rack and having to sort through all of them is NOT my thing. Some people are bargain shoppers. Some people get anxiety in disorganized stores packed of stuff. I'm the latter. Do I wish I were an amazing bargain hunter? Sure. But it's just not me. If you're a bargain hunter, this might be a goldmine for you. For me, it was just stress and no purchases.

This location is very busy, so the messiness of the store proves it. I don't think I have ever been in a ROSS where anything is in order (particularly women's shoes). If you need a specific size, it's best to start in the smallest and work your way there because no one seems to keep up with the clutter. I do think the selection is wonderful and prices are good, but it's such a disjointed store that it's getting 3 stars. It's the thrift store of department stores.

The Center City Ross usually has a good selection of bath and body products - nice shampoos, lotions and washes at really good prices.  The clothes tend to be hit or miss -- more often a miss, but with the occasional really good hit.  The staff can be hit or miss, too, running the gamut from screaming at/to each other and ignoring customers to being really jovial and helpful.  Bottom line for me is that good things can be had here but you'd better have the patience to really dig through racks and shelves, and maybe to wait in a long line when checking out.

In and out of different Ross locations all of the time. Love to feel like I'm getting a great deal when I'm shopping. I can find something for just about every member of my family including the dog! Housewares, clothes, shoes, jewelry, accessories, lingerie, chairs, dishes, towels, toys, whatever you need, you can most likely find it at Ross. Sometimes customer service is less than desirable...
Was very disappointed that this particular Ross had no maternity section. Very low selection on kid clothes too.

When you just enter the store, it smells like an extremely dirty bathroom.. Once you're in though.. I can't imagine how I've never been to a Ross store all this while..  I went there for a bag, and they have an extensive collection of bags. MK and CK totes and crossbody bags are up for a steal! I scored a CK bag for $30. A way better deal all than I would've gotten elsewhere even after applying coupons.. I just walked by the clothes section though, and it's a hot mess. I couldn't imagine digging in the rubble of piled up clothes. Overall, if they spruced up their racks and used some air freshener, it would be an instant hit! Will definitely be back for more bags.. and more.. and more!!
Kickass Converse for 10 dollars. Can't knock that!

Today had bad experiences.The staff today had absolutely no problem or customer service skills.A Pair of black pants didn't have A price.Went to customer service to get A price. To spare the details about the incompetency; The result ended in me having to go and find a pair of pants with that name brand,and bring it back to the costumer service. What the hell! I am not on the payroll there.two managers,one helping out at the cash registers because of long line,the other just unapproachable. Tell you what,I was very upset because those pants were perfect fit,style, material,and I would have walked out with A smile instead of disbelief.one star just because the store was open.

Does this location even deserve 1 star? The lines are INCREDIBLY long all the time. They will have 30+ people in line(seriously) with 2 cash registers open. Walk around and what do you see?? 4 or 5 "employees" straightening head bands or belts. Basically doing NOTHING  to help with the line. I will NEVER go back to this store. Every time I have tried to shop there the lines have been horrible, the place is so dirty, and incredibly unorganized. Who ever is in charge of this Ross location evidentially does not care at all about keeping business, customer service, or over all cleanliness. Yuck!

The store is a mess! They had dirty clothes, I'm taking pink baby outfits covered in black grime hanging on racks to be sold.  When we did finally find a couple good items for a friends baby shower, we head to the register and get behind next person in line. When they leave my daughter starts to put the stuff on the counter. The cashier walks away and then goes over to her co worker hangs out for a bit and then comes by the reg again and turns off the light and walks away never to return. At which point the returns lady calls the person behind us up and starts ringing them up. Not one word said to me during this entire 10 min thing. I dropped the stuff and took my daughter crying out of the store trying to explain to her why we were not getting her toy.  I was half tempted to walk out with the stuff that I was trying to buy! I will never be visiting this store again! Wow!
I am a huge fan of ross!I love finding cute shoes for cheap!The only problem I have here is it's a huge mess.Nothings every organized

Typical Ross you'll find in other states. They do hold a lot more options of women's clothes like shirts, dresses, and skirts. They hold a lot of iconic brand items like Disney and Marvel. There other selection of home goods,  toys, etc was a different story. Prices are cheap as usual. It's close to their Walmart and other shopping centers.

Every time I come to this store, the lines are outrageously long and there's always someone either rude or not even paying attention working the dressing room. I guess I just settled thinking this was how they operate, and come on my days off (when standing in line forever matters slightly less). What's worse is, they typically have only one, 2 if you're lucky, cashiers working at any given time. I really love it when they have 5 or 6 employees working on hangers or whatever while the line is 20-30 minutes long. Last night I was treated so poorly, I will NEVER return to this location. (I come at least once a week). As everyone knows, Ross isn't exactly known for its organization...so when I grabbed a pair of shorts, thinking they were labeled "S", and on a rack with all the other smalls, and didn't even think twice about trying them on, I was a little irritated when I got home and found that they were actually a size 5. Woops. No big deal, I just had to find another outfit to put together, and I'd just return them. I have never had a problem in my entire life returning ANY purchase-even without receipts you can get a store credit at almost any store.  However, last night I came to this Ross with my receipt, shorts WITH ALL THE TAGS STILL ON THEM, and original bag they were tossed in just TWO DAYS PRIOR. When I walked through the front door, there were at least 20 people-if not more-standing in line. I made a face of surprise, and the cashier Amanda at the front said "Should know better thinking you could just run in here" and laughed. I thought it was really weird of her to say, but I went ahead and got in line since I had driven out of my way to return these. 20 minutes pass by of people who don't understand personal space while I'm standing in line, and t's finally my turn. I approach AMANDA'S register, after she had wasted my and everyone else's time in line chatting it up with the ladies in front of me, and say hello. She pulls the shorts and receipt out of my bag and makes this face as if she just opened a dirty diaper. She asked me if I had a cat. I said 'no do I look like a cat person?' And giggled. She then says "I am not returning these. You clearly put these on a dog or something." I then calmly tell her that I thought these would fit and got home, realized they don't. She said 'so was there anything wrong with these?' and I said 'No they just didn't work'...she then says "So there's nothing wrong with them, but you want to return them?"..at this point I'm thinking "WTF, Do I need to give a written statement or something when returning an item??"...I said "I'm just trying to return them, they didn't work. I tried them on and they don't work. That's all." She then tells me I am clearly trying to pull one over on her and wore them. (PLEASE keep in mind at this point that not only is the ROSS tag still on these, but the brand tag that sits over the hip is still on these, and that I would've had to go on stage wearing these, and that's a ridiculous assertion). I just stood there totally confused...and she said "look these have little wrinkles right here, you clearly wore these"...At this point, my blood is boiling and I've already started mentally typing out this online review, and I tell her 'this line is really long, and you're trying to confront me because I didn't steam, iron and press, then lint roll these stupid shorts? You're kidding right?"...She said 'I can take this shirt back in here if I can check to see it hasn't been worn but these shorts were worn'...SO, I ask for my crap back, throw it in the bag...drive 30 minutes to the next Ross, walk in, am greeted warmly with no line, and was given a refund immediately with no questions asked. HOW HARD WAS THAT AND WHY DID I NEED TO BE QUESTIONED LIKE I WAS ON TRIAL! THEY WERE $10 SHORTS!... AMANDA....you have no business ever confronting, questioning, or accusing a customer of anything....if you even suspected someone was up to no good, you get a manager..or loss prevention..you NEVER start a debate..it's not your job to police people. You're there to provide a friendly face and complete transactions. That's it. I am so insulted and will never return here EVER again.

I only go in here when I have some time to waste... and I mean a LOT of time. It's a big disorganized chaos, but I suppose it's worth it to find a good deal. I usually stick to the perimeter of the store and avoid the clothing section. Digging through disorganized racks is bad enough. Feeling like you're going through airport security upon entering the fitting room just makes it worse.  I've purchased luggage, bed sheets, kids shoes, kitchen items, and more here... all heavily discounted below what you would typically pay at a department store. And, higher quality stuff than you would find at Target/Walmart. It takes a bit of effort, and definitely a lot of time, but it can be worthwhile.

Was not impressed with this store, my first time in a Ross store. At this location they follow and watch you to see if you are stealing, even though the store has more cameras than the Secret service!! And clothes were not as cheap as I was expecting, alot of the sneakers are knockoffs, ugggghh!!!

The last time I  shopped at this Ross , it was OK,  I visited the Ross on City line Ave, Stay Away!! The shelves are never stocked, the place is always messy and the workers could seem to care less! Not a good place to shop .
My most recent visit was better than the last. The store was very clean. However, everything was so spread out and inventory was minimal. My question was when are they closing the store?

Success! It's nearly impossible for me to find fashionable plus size clothing at a discount store and this trip was particularly important as I needed to dress for a job interview. I was lucky enough to find a designer shirt in my size that looks professional but can also be dressed down. I love the clothes they have here and the other merchandise(especially their candle selection), I just wish they had larger sizes when it comes to the shoes. I have large feet as I'm a tall lady and they have really cute stuff just never in my size! Aside from that this place is great!

Even though this location is kind of far I don't mind the drive because this location has way more than the others on my side of town. I went today while waiting on a friend for lunch and found about 3 pairs of shoes I couldn't walk away from! The location was well stocked in every section and there's so many good deals on everything.

This Ross is a little confusing since it spans across two retail units. If you enter off of 7th street, the women's section is to the right and the men's section is to the left.   That's the general rule of thumb, but the electronics and fitness sections were on the left side with the men's clothing.   Once I got my bearings the confusion was worth it because I was able to find a running belt for $7. That wasn't happening in a sporting goods store. The selection was slim pickings and they had what they had.   With the hit or miss nature of the products, you'll walk out loving or hating it. It's worth a shot if you are looking for something at a discount or just want to browse without any specific goal in mind.

Ross is what it is. You go here for a deal. And, deals they have. But it's a hodge podge of a place. You really need to weave your way through the trinkets, random goodies, and what not. And, sometimes they have something you really like in one size, but not your size. They often get inventory in that is never restocked, but rather replaced by the next thing they get at a price that allows them to sell it at a discount.  But you don't go hear for a high quality experience. You go here for the hodge podge of a deal place that it is.  My wife and I got what we needed and the price was right.  The one thing I found weird about this location is that the men's side and women's side are like two different stores. We had to pull a "let's meet in the middle" when we're both done route.  But hey, you sort of get what you pay for at Ross.

Ross has had just what I needed on a budget more than once. The inside isn't glamorous.  But the selection for my needs even for a formal dress in a rush and under $20.00 has made it a stop for me and my friends.

This is probably the worst Ross I have ever been to.  I have been to all the ones in town, as well as some in San Diego, Phoenix, Oahu, LA, etc. It is a decent sized store, but it is never well organized....even if you go first thing in the morning. ^__^ Not only is everything in disarray, but they don't seem to have as much merchandise as other locations. Their home goods selection is especially lacking. Customer service is okay, but not as friendly as other locations. And definitely not as friendly as the staff from TJ Maxx and Marshalls!  I would drop by this Ross if I happened to be shopping at the Pier 1 Imports next door, but I won't go out of my way. ^__^

I don't think this Ross is that bad, especially for a discount store in Philadelphia. This Ross has a really good selection of housewares, specifically kitchen stuff. Skip over the clothing section, but check out the shoes, sometimes they have Steve Madden stuff.

The stars are for my friend's shopping experience. She found numerous cute and adorable dresses. That was the highlight for her. She also found some cute casual sweaters,shirts and active wear. We went there twice while in Philly because she thought she got good deals. We met two women in Reading Terminal who suggested this place. They weren't lying!  The men's clothing and shoe section weren't as good as the women's section.

It's in a strip mall with Home Goods, Michaels, Lane Bryant and a bicycle shop.  I have never been to a Ross before, but figured it was like a TJ Maxx or Marshalls....um, I think NOT.  There was a security guard at the front door-sketchy...made me not want to enter.  The store was a mess....stuff tossed of shelves and yet the racks were pretty barren.  I saw only off brands, no name brands and the quality of the clothing looked very poor....ie. synthetic matieral.  They had shoes, none that tickeled my fancy, clothing (men's, women's, kids, plus, petite, maternity) home decorations, bath items, kitchen items, men and women's frangrances.  Some people must like it because there were people shopping.  Good for them, but count me out.

3.5...Hit or miss and usually longer lines (HINT go to the men's side for a shorter line) It really is fun to walk through and browse to see what they have...  I love me some bargain shopping and they have a ton of items even including luggage (wish I would have known that before I got my ugly green set from K Mart). It isn't the cleanest store and the employees leave a little to be desired that is for sure. But look for what it is, this place is great and convenient (right of the 8th and Market Septa/Patco lines)  There is a restroom back by the ladies fitting room, but was out of order when I went. As for shoes, if you are a size 11 or higher - don't bother lol!

I go to this place atleast once a month, and I have been a customer since 2008. I like the baby clothing and toys  section. I do find some good brands  for almost half of their original price once in a while. However, there are times that there in almost no inventory and I barely see baby cloths or toys.    One thing that I can always find here is my favorite  purse. I almost bought all of my purses here.  There are some other household goods, like curtains, carpets,  kithchen stuff, some beuty products,  shoes. But some times the inventory is to the minimum.    As for the store, it is  not a very organize store and the lines  for checkout get very long sometimes. The stuff are ok and some( but not all) are professional.  When it comes to  returns, always have your recept with you and make sure what you have bought is not being used atall. They are kinda strict for returns.  All in one, I think the store could and should be more well managed and organized...with all that I would recommend checking out Ross, and I think It worths checking it out. You may find pretty good stuff for very discounted prices.

Unlike another reviewer, I have shopped here within the last 10 years.  In fact, I shop at Ross fairly often. There are 4 local to me but I always prefer the one on Market Street in Philly.  I have to present myself in a professional manner at work. To go out to a department store and buy a suit, I am looking at spending $100-$250 each if there is a sale at Macy's.  Maybe some of you can afford 10-20+ suits at that price, and thats fine.  However, I can (and do) get great suits and suit separates for a fraction of the price.  I'm talking $10-$50. Sometimes I need to make a few alterations for better fit, but I own a sewing machine and can drive my car to my alteration specialist.  I've also bought casual clothes, shoes, etc there.  Everything has held up wonderfully for me, and I'd have to say Ive been shopping there for almost 10 years now. Nothing has fallen apart on me, nothing has disinigrated in my washer or dryer.   It's not always true that you can get things at the outlets for the same or cheaper price.  In fact, quality at outlet stores has completely   changed and you may find the better quality item at Ross. Many outlet stores now run their own lines and no longer take the markdowns and clearance from their name brand stores. That's right, outlet stores are starting to make cheaper clothing with cheaper materials that resemble their normal pricey stuff, and consumers buy it up like they are getting good deals.  I've had far more clothing from outlets fall apart than Ross.

I introduced my man to ROSS and he loved it!!! We just got our first house and he bought a bunch of pictures and kitchen knives. The doc aisle is my favorite! They have toys for half the price and great deals just all around! I recommend you coming here for clothes, bathroom, kitchen, gifts and etc. before anywhere else! We will be back for sure!

This Ross is just kind of lame.  It's got the same selection of other's Ross's but that's all it's got going for it.  The parking lot feels kind of sketchy. There were overflowing trash cans everywhere outside. Inside it was super busy.  The dressing room seriously smelled like a baby's diaper.
