I still think Friday mornings is the best time to go, because they have the new stuff out but it hasn't been picked over by the weekend crowd.

LOVE ROSS!!! Santa Barbara is known for there high fashion ways and with a college budget I find amazing deals here from shoes to great accessories. I always look here before heading over to a high retail store. They also have great frames and home decorations. Can't beat the prices!!!! It's a must shop here!!

Ross always has something to entice me to break out the wallet. To keep my "want, need, gotta haves" in check, I shop with a list and blinders on. Check out lines can be a nightmare, so be prepared to spend the time, and bargain hunters can elbow you in the isles if you aren't paying attention. I prefer early ams or just before closing to shop when I can. As a geezer, Tuesdays offer me a discount--one of the many benefits of aging!
Ugh is about the sum of this store horrible staff god forbid u ask for help or try to spend your money !!! Never again, take myself to Burington coat factory , marshals or To TJ  Max .

This store has a good selection with full shelves, unlike other Ross I have been to. The lines are long as usual. Only 2 registers open but that's to be expected at Ross. The employees seem very nice.
The staff was fairy nice to be around. Great sales.. I bought a huge Nike umbrella for $3!

My favorite Ross! This is my third time here and I am continuously impressed. I arrived around 11 AM on a Sunday. Parking was not hard to find.   Pros: Always clean and organized; never busy - which means no long lines and no one crowding me while I raid the racks; lots of fitting rooms; excellent customer service  Cons: (more of a con for me personally) Junior women's seems to have more medium and large tops compared to small - however, I still seem to find cute stuff! This is no deal breaker for me.   Today's experience: I visited every section on the left hand side of the store (juniors, kitchen, decor, bath, shoes, bags). Clean and organized everywhere. I used the fitting room and tried on 8+ items. They allow 8 at a time so I had to leave some out and come back for the rest.   I interacted with four people today. Security, who greeted me as I walked in and as I left. An employee who walked pass me, who said good morning. The woman at the fitting rooms, who was very nice and understanding about all of the clothes I was trying on. And the man at the register, who was also nice and explained the return policy to me when I asked. All around excellent customer service.   Past experiences: Just as satisfying as today. I have done a return with a receipt. It was quick and easy. Customer service has always been good for me.   Overall: Highly recommend and will continue coming back to this location.

Buying bed sheets and all of the prices for the bed sheets have the same prices and when I was paying for them, they told me the prices in there were wrong and it's twice the price on the tag so I decided not to get them. When I was walking out the door, I overheard them that the prices on the tags were correct and they didn't even tell me.

Looking for a nice decorative planter for my cube I decieded to check and see if Ross had one, for they are known to be a lot less than anywhere else. Not only did I find a beautiful ceramic pot for $12 normally $35 I found lots of dress shirts like Kenneth Cole, Pierre Cardin, Ralph Lauren for about $9-$13!! So stocked I found this store, I love saving $$$ This store is super clean and everything is nicely put away. I didn't even feel like I was in a Ross store. You simply cannot ask for more!!

I love Ross for all of the items they have at a lower price than its competitors. But the past two times I've been to this location, there has only been one cashier and the line goes all the way back to the aisles. It has taken about 10-15 mintues to get through the line before. I've also noticed multiple employees standing or walking around that could be called up to the front as back up cashieers. I wouldn't reccomend going here if you're in a hurry or on a schedule.
The place looks like a Third World garage sale.   Unfriendly staff including one who either refused to talk to me in English or didn't speak it in the first place.

For that business and fashion savvy women, this store always has a great variety of pants suits and handbags. The store is ALWAYS clean and during my recent visit I was blown away with their Valentines display. The people are so friendly and always greets everyone that walks through the door. One of the things that does bother me are the number of unaccompanied children running around under the clothes, opening and playing with the toys. Its like parents just tell them to go play while they shop. I often see the employees running around trying to prevent the kids from opening the toys and urging them to stay with their parents. To those parents why would you allow your kids to open and play with the toys and you don't plan on paying for them? Some of us would like to buy unopened and unplayed toys, wouldn't you? Hats off to the employees committed to keeping this store clean and that's why this is my favorite Ross. You should check'em out!!

The best thing about this store is the location in close proximity to Albertsons so I can get all my shopping done at once. They do not seem to stock items in a timely fashion, when I came here just the other day, many shelves were barren. They also have a smaller hair products/skincare section than most of the Ross stores that I have been to. They are open late for the holidays!

I love Ross and all their very affordable items but this store in particular has some of the worst customer service/management. To me it's important to receive great service wherever I'm giving my business and the employees here cannot provide that.

Great store for housewares, not so great on clothes.  Each time I have been here I have had luck finding items for lower prices than elsewhere. I spent only $25 total throw pillows, a jewelry tree, hand weights, a coffee cup, and a lunchbox.  I have found much better clothes at the Market st location.

Dresses galore - gimme, gimme! I have a slight dress fetish and Ross in Goleta knows how to meet my demands. All under $15 - retailed anywhere from $30-$120. Where else can you get brand names, brand new, decent quality and a diverse selection? Kitchen selection is great and the athletic wear is as well. And can't forget about the shoes..ahh, the shoes..every time I go, it's always clean and organized vs. the upper State St. location. All around one stop shop for affordable clothing and house goodies.
Good place to pick up towels and random kitchen supplies. Usually can find what you are looking for...

While there are great prices, I find that shopping here is more of a hassle than it is worth. The store is always lacking enough employees although the employees who are there are very nice. The shoes are my biggest issue. They are all held together by a security tag. While I understand this is important, it makes it impossible to walk in the shoes and get a good feel for them. On top of that, I've tried on multiple pairs where the shoes were connected with the right shoe on the left side and vice versa. I can't try on both shoes at once which is really annoying. To top it all off, I bought a pair of sandals which now have a sticky residue on the heel because Ross put a sticker on fabric. I used to love Ross but my recent experiences at this one are ruining my love for the store.

I've decided that paying more than $10 for flats is a waste of money since I end up walking through them so quickly.   Ross is the perfect solution. I almost always find cute flats either on clearance or I'll even sometimes pitch in the extra couple bucks for regularly priced shoes.   This Ross is definitely better than the one back home and I have found some great finds here.   When people ask me where I get *insert product,* I have been known to occasionally utter embarrassingly their slogan,  "I got it at Ross"

Extremely rude employees. The person serving me did not bother to carefully fold my clothes, which were silk and linen (i.e. easily wrinkled). When I insisted on folding them myself because clearly I could not trust her to do so, she became rude and uncooperative. Before leaving the store, I pointed out to her that she had a terrible attitude, but I was ignored. Employees today do not care about providing good service - it's not as if this employee will get fired for making customers unhappy, even if I knew the employee's name and published it.

Sometimes I find great deals, other times not so much. The store is usually well kept.  They do have a limit which means I buy less.  I don't like to make more than one trip to the fitting room.  Therefore,  whatever is over their limit, I don't bother trying on which means I won't even consider buying it. The staff is USUALLY friendly.

Not even a one star unfortunately Jane I believe her name was, not only Rude but poor customer service, she rushed us out of the transaction , my family smiled and was sweet with her as I observed the whole transaction. My Father thanked her for the transaction said " have a good day " she rolled her eyes and yelled " next !" Not only was the transaction was cold but someone like that doesn't need to be in retail. Don't waste your time. The stock is terrible, the place is understaffed and clearly not motivated- and the last time I was out there, I promised myself I'd never go again. And I won't. It's sad and scary how much plastic and polyester crap is cluttering up the place, with little if any decent-quality merchandise available. Virtually every aisle had merchandise laying on the floor, creating not only a safety hazard but an impossible shopping experience. I brought this to the attention of the barely-old-enough-to-vote manager on duty, and the deer-in-the-headlights look in his eyes left me with precious little confidence that my concerns would ever be addressed. The women's clothing racks are skimpy at best, ridiculously bare at worst. If you don't love polyester, you might as well not even bother looking. The Five Points store is better stocked; but still, that's not saying much, unless you REALLY like polyester.  The security guards have a bigger presence than the sales people. There's a bare minimum of checkout clerks working, which I can understand, because it's rare that there are ever more than a couple of people in line, winding their way through a labyrinth of candy and plastic water bottles for sale, to tempt your crying children while you wait. On rare occasions when they first opened, you used to be able to find some decent housewares, a wall mirror, artwork- and at the perfectly right time even some bargains on shoes.  But nowadays, the shoes are wired up with so many anti-theft tags, cords and wires that a bomb squad would have trouble untangling them. There is apparently no simple way to try a pair of shoes on and take a short walk in them, without going to the checkout lines first and waiting until you can get someone to 'cut the cords' for you.  It's a shame, really. The concept was good at one time, but nowadays everything seems to have gone downhill in the search for the cheapest goods to be sold at the cheapest price, while paying your employees the least possible wages, unconcerned about their low morale (...and yes, I talked several of them; they're miserable, but "a job is a job", especially in this town), and the omnipresent highest concern for preventing theft.  And if you're wondering where the plastic that's choking our oceans literally to death is coming from, look at the products and the packaging in this store.  When do we say "enough"?
