Meh. I'm always kind of disappointed with Ross. Two stars because my mom left her cell phone here and they kept it safe. Lol

Not really sure why this store is even open - every time I have gone in half the racks are empty and the store looks like it had gotten ransacked by elephants. My first experience with a Ross Dress for Less was about 16 years ago when I was living in Philly. There was one located downtown and I would love to go on weekends and find awesome deals. Plus it was huuuuge. So when I heard there was one coming to Indy I was super excited cause the prices were so good. But this location has been quite a disappointment. Like I said, the racks and shelves are half empty and so disorganized. I was in just yesterday and saw some cute shoes - but only 3-4 pairs of them. So I thought I would check the racks and they only went up to 8 1/2. What happened to sizes 9, 9 1/2 and 10?   The beauty section is minimal, with random brand names, and ones you would find at Wal-Mart. A lot of bottles were already open and used and nothing made any sense. The kitchen section is lacking, with only a few pots and pans here and there. I should have just gone to TJ Maxx across the street. But they always have 30-45 minute long lines to cash out, even during the middle of the weekday. So, if you don't want to wait in line and have some time to browse through the store for some bargain hunting, by all means stop by Ross. But don't expect to find as much as you would from other discount stores.

This store is pretty hit or miss but you can find some good deals with patience. They recently rearranged the store so shoes are now in with clothing for their respective audiences. The store is still cluttered and the shelves aren't neat. Lines are long and there never seem to be more then two cashiers on at a time. A large number of the women's dressing room doors are broken so I would reccomend trying stuff on at home and returning what doesn't fit. There's now an Amazon box in the store but it's not turned on. If you're a bargain hunter with patience this is a decent store to visit. If you're looking for a quick in and out or a quiet shopping experience go to the Ross in Bensalem instead.

I have absolutely no idea where they got the first 7 pictures but I can sure as hell tell you that that is NOT this Ross. The last two pictures are more accurate. This store is completely trashy. The employees aren't friendly at all and most of the patrons are rude and ignorant. I will never go back to this location again.

that cashier and that shitty manager Thomas told me that they cant sell me the items that was priced and scanned for ,49 coz they said it    wasnt described as the it should be.  i said as a customer i should pay for what is tagged and scanned and Thomas tokd me to call the corporate office to complain coz Ross have their own policy and whatever prices tagged and scanned on the items if they said they wont sell it then they wont. mind you the top already have 4 different pink sticker on it already. and the cashier said she can sold it to me for $7.99 if i want it after 20% discount.  can anybody tell me i was wrong for insisting to pay the tagged and scanned price??

This Ross establishment was complete and utter trash. As soon as I came in my senses were tingly... something was off. I usually shop in order so that I never miss anything worth noticing. But, sadly I missed a lot because all the rows were intensely disorganized. Clothes were mixed up with the bathroom section and makeup mixed up with shoes. This Ross looked like a teenagers room after a whole week has passed.   Once I finished my shopping, I went to check out. I was flabbergasted to hear the cashier say, "Can you take the hangers off and hang them behind you?". WHAT!?!? No one shops and works at the same time. After I told her that I wasn't going to be doing her job she muffled roughly under her voice and stormed off with the hangers. She came back, never looked me in the face and finished checking me out.   Never again will I step foot at this Ross.

What is even going on at this store? They're not remodeling. There's no information on the door about their lack of merchandise. It was a waste for me to drive 20 minutes to this store. Usually it's just in messy shambles, but to just not have much of anything in multiple aisles? UGH.

It's Ross .... It's nice that they have security inside when u think someone s employed but the management needs to find a better way to prevent the loss other than placing a security guard right when u walk in .. it's not like it's a bank ...it's a store providing deals .. place RFID tags  already ...

POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE! GHETTO!  I was charged twice by someone claiming to be the manager...when I called to speak to her about it...I was told it was up to me to dispute the transaction with my bank when she told me the first transaction didn't go through and I need to swipe my card again. I made up my mind never to shop here again.  Used to shop here several times a week...I'll find somewhere else to spend my money.

I had heard rumors about Ross having some crazy clearance going on of "after Christmas stock." I've never been to a Ross before, but I'm a huge fan of discount stores. In need of  birthday gifts for the hubs, I decided to check it out.   While I didn't see any crazy clearance deals that impressed me, I did find a lot of great stuff with great prices. I had to check out the shelves of discounted beauty products, and found lots of reasonably priced goodies. Just nothing that struck my fancy. There was a little bit of everything, from high end moisturizers to vitamins and makeup.  The mens section, which was what I was after, is considerably smaller than the womens section. There was also not much of a childrens section. The store is predominantly women's clothing and accessories and home goods.  The store is organized nicely and gives a first impression of a department-ish store, rather than the messy discount store look you often find in stores as such. I was able to find 2 really nice shirts for my husband that typically retail around $60 for $12.99 a piece. I also found one of his favorite colognes that retails for a little over $100, but paid $18 for it. Great deals!

I bought 4 items and needed to return one of the items, and that item is a brown bag. The cashier, whose name is Naomi, had a bad attitude to begin with, and refunded my money as another item by mistake, which has a lower price. I pointed out her mistake and she insisted that's the right item. I requested the manager, he brought his security with him as if I'm a criminal. He simply said because it is the only item that says "brown" on the receipt, as the bag I'm returning happens to be brown, so she chose to return that item as if she did the right thing. I explained to him that the brown bag I am returning didn't have a tag, so the cashier at that time ring that item up as a different color, that is why it says a black bag rather than brown on the receipt for my returning item, but his stubborn numb head refuses to think outside the box, and now I have to suffer for their incompetency and couldn't return my item. Never been into a store where the manager is as messed up as his employee. This store really need to hire people that know what they are doing, or it will get ruined by these low lives really fast.
Literally stood in line for 55 minutes. 2 registers open and and line was as far as the end of the men's department. The store is an absolute mess. Not one worker said hello. Ridiculous.
This location is a little "rough."  Staff not at all helpful, racks are so crammed with merchandise it's difficult to look through them.  Lines are long and cashiers are painfully slow.

Deplorable cashier!  She was so rude and snitty I couldn't believe they are so desperate to hire this kind of scum!!  Do they ever train these people to face the public?  I may never return to this store due to this experience.  Furthermore...very dirty and messy.  I had to literally pull the hand wipes through the container to grasp some for the shopping cart.  The so-called security guard stood there and watched me without offering a hand while I proceeded into this store
This place is a MESS!!! Over crowded and just messy. Everything on the floor. Things were opened and missing. I walked in and around and walked back out.

It's really hard to review Ross and expect something that just blows your mind away. It's Ross...they have something for everyone. This store in particular has a lot of stuff. I am talking two-tier racks of men clothing, a wall of shoes PLUS more shelves for shoes. Everything is unorganized but it's really hard to expect the staff to clean all that stuff every single time they get a chance. This store is just too busy. I feel they would benefit from lessening their inventory so you could actually browse through their clothes/shoes. I am sure this store just continues to get messy as the day goes by. This in turn makes it difficult for you to really through what they have. My advise would be to get here as early as possible for a cleaner store. By the end of the day you'll get discouraged trying to rummage through the mess.   All in all, it's still Ross. You are going to find a good deal, as long as you actually do find what you are looking for.

I visited on a weekend and I love this location. I am pleased that the loss prevention agent presumed my innocence instead of presuming my guilt.  If you go make time to go to Chopsticks Buffet for lunch. Lunch is only $8.59 per person Mondays to Saturdays. There is also Thai food next door, Subway, Sally Beauty Supply, Tuesday Morning, Dollar Tree, and Rainbow's nearby.  I will definitely return.

Ross is the part of the THX company which includes; TJ Maxx, Marshall's and Ross. I really love this company and I am a stockholder. They opened 70 new stores in 2018.  Whenever I'm at one of these stores they are always packed. Online shopping has become super popular of late and I buy something almost every day online. But there is something about actually going into a store and feeling, touching and trying things on before you buy it.  My most favorite thing is that you never know what products they will have in stock each time. I like the treasure hunt feel of this store. I purchased so many random things that I needed.  This location was very neat, clean and organized!

This store is great! I went for business attire and business casual attire, and they had amazing slacks, blouses, dresses, etc. They did not have any skirts, though, which was frustrating. I ended up buying some of the best fitted joggers, and they seem to have endless racks of clothes to go through. I ended up buying more than what I originally came for.

I wasn't terribly thrilled with Ross. I plan I giving them another shot, but upon our first visit, we were shopping for Special Needs ladies for a chaperoned summer trip. Their plus size availability was dismal. It was mainly work out pants. We had to have those two ladies wait until we went to a different store, like Cato, so we could find them appropriate outfits. My biggest complaint was trying on clothing. As staff, each of us was assigned to two ladies. Because two were plus sized and had nothing to try on, we had three staff members to help four ladies. However, we were absolutely smothered by the staff and security at the dressing rooms. I understand controlling loss. However, because we needed to but three full outfits for each lady and had multiple options for both tops and bottoms, the incredibly strict number of items made this a very difficult trip. We didn't want to steal anything! We just wanted to compare the blue and black tops!  You also couldn't be IN the dressing room without a number on a card saying how many items you have. We were assisting ladies with special needs that needed help putting certain things on or whatnot. Because they were changing it was difficult to switch pieces in and out to keep our number of items IN the dressing room to six or less, and by insisting we have the "number of items" card while in the dressing room, we finally had to have all three staff with one lady at a time. We couldn't take the "0" "number of items" card outside of the dressing room with us, so when I ventured out into the store for a replacement top and came back to a totally different attendant, I got to explain myself and the situation all over again. The folks at Burlington also preferred six items or less but understood what we were doing AND the situation and worked with us. They were present but not hovering, overbearing, and difficult to work with. Stopping at Ross added an extra hour and a half to our trip merely because of the hoop jumping in the dressing room.

Went to Ross expecting to spend some time there shopping for clothing. Went through the racks with in 20 minutes and only found about 6 things to try on went into the dressing rooms and was not impressed By the dressing assistants customer service tried everything on and only one thing fit right. I come out of the dressing room and hung my stuff on the racks deciding to get one thing. The dressing room attendant rushed over to count my stuff and I stood there patiently waiting. Then she says that I'm missing something. I say I shouldn't be and she counts again then again then again before she realizes she missed something. If you can't count right and carefully you shouldn't have that job. I have never felt so humiliated in my life. She ended up apologizing and saying to have a nice day but I will not be going there again.   They barely have any selection and look like they are going out of business the employees I have seen don't go out of their way to provide customer service and the dressing room attendant was about to accuse me of stealing even when everything was hung up in front of her.   There are several other Ross stores in the area that are much more worth the trip.
Cheap prices, wouldn't buy there electronics, or food stuffs. Clothes is good quality for the most part and they have some good deals, sometimes they have some nice sneakers in stock.

Oh my I just encountered the scariest loss prevention person ever. My shopping experience should not be uncomfortable. I was so ready to get out of there.  The lines are always so ridiculous is a main reason I don't go. Much rather go to Burlington. Prices aren't as good as they should be for the quality.

This location is relatively close to other store so it is a convenience pick for me. I generally prefer to shop elsewhere.   The day I stopped in I found a few good discounts, the store seemed unorganized and messy overall.   My friend and I were patiently waiting in line when the security guard asked us if we were with the people ahead of us in line. We said no and then the security guard asked us to move back in line to give the people ahead of us some space.. We were not doing anything wrong just waiting in line. Due to the security guard being so belligerent and rude, we got out of line put our merchandise back on the shelf and walked out. Customer Service is terrible at this location.   This is the last time I will go to this store location and the chain itself should consider hiring less rude employees. My money will be spent elsewhere.

You have to keep in mind that this is a discount store so you kind of have to search through many things to find one thing that you like. But the prices make it an even trade. For me anyway. However. This Ross store has by far the rudest employees. If they aren't chatting amongst themselves about things I'd rather not hear about, they are ignoring you. When I asked for some help I received a very snarky "hold on". If you hate your job that much, work somewhere else! Don't take your disgust with your life's choices out on me.

This is the strangest Ross Dress For Less I have ever visited.   As for most RDFL stores, it's in a strip mall -- no surprise there.  The store is so sparsely stocked that it has the look of a place that is imminently going out of business. The racks are disconcertingly empty, and the space between the racks and displays is so broad that you wonder if they just experienced a run on cheap polyester-blend t-shirts, or if the store is always that way?  Housewares are sparsely stocked, beauty is sparsely stocked...heck, *everything* is sparsely stocked. It was spooky. I looked around briefly and left. Really, there is no reason to shop here.
Me fascina esta tienda!!! Es la mejor!!! Siempre encuentro algo nuevo y diferente a precio razonable. De todas las localidades esta es la mejor.

Super busy since they just opened Saturday. No help in sight and customers out the wazoo... I'd wait a few weeks until the crowds die down. Great prices. I ended up going in to check it out and came out with a toddler chair for $59.99. Some of the stuff is super cute. And they carry Juicy Couture. One of my favs.

It's a great place to buy inexpensive dresses and sweaters. But the lines are too long. They also have shoes delivered pretty frequently, so that's good. I'm giving it 3 stars because you find things that last but nothing really sensational- like high end fashion for cheap. They have good brands, though, and good prices, but nothing spectacular.

Very disappointed in this location. Although I understand that this mall has much less to offer these days, people still shop here. The selection is terrible and you only have 2 portable fitting rooms!!!

I'm not crazy about Ross but this one seemed to at least be a little better organized than other ones I have been to. Ross doesn't seem to have to have as good quality clothing as similar places like TJ maxx or marshalls. Also, it always seems like they never having any clothing in a 0 or XS which is frustrating. I have found a couple good deals here before though.

The northwest Reno Ross store is clean and easy to navigate. The sales clerks are nice and my return was processed easily. The security guard greeted me when I entered the store and I had no problem when I asked to use the restroom. Very nice store!

Pretty basic rose. Neat for the most part. Things are pretty organized and easy to find. I was looking for shoes and was surprised to find some pretty pricy shoes there for a super great deal. I don't buy em is I didn't need em. But still, this place will definitely save you money?
The store has ok pricing but its very badly organized. I was looking for a regualr t-shirt and i found a shirt in a pair of jeans

Good products but one downside; I would have given an additional star but one unpleasant experience knocked them down a notch. I purchased a small piece of furniture along with a few other items, but was shopping solo, I  asked for assistance to place the item in my car, since they have those non-exit poles on the shopping carts. They refused to help or get staff member to help stating a liability. My opinion, DON'T SELL LARGE FURNITURE ITEMS IF YOU CAN'T ACCOMMODATE THE CUSTOMER TO LOAD. #rediculousness In my opjnion.

This location has great options in the home department. I think the furniture and home decor section is one of the largest for Ross Stores in Tucson. However, their clothing section is about the same or smaller than other Ross locations. It was pretty understaffed each time I've visited, but that could have something to do with there being less traffic at the Foothills Mall.

If there's anything this store is, it's consistent... Consistently terrible, that is.  -Long lines always with one cashier. -Dirty floors.  -SLOW service. Is anyone who works here concerned about the 15+ people in line? -Unpleasant customer service, is anyone here happy ever? There's never a thank you or a smile. Even eye contact seems foreign.  I had to at least give 2 stars because their home & shoe collection, while disorganized, has some gems. You're better off going to TJ Maxx a few stores over.

This particular store isn't as well stocked as others I've visited, but as usual, I found some killer deals!  Most important to me, is the friendly staff.  The gals at this store were very accommodating.  Will go there often!

What David said, "What Ross sells is inexpensive. The workers probably do not make a good hourly. And the store conditions probably aren't the most talked about feature to keep customers coming back."  If the store conditions depress you, go booze up at the Wine and Liquor store next door before you come.  It's a Ross!  The Jan Brady to its sister store Marshalls and the Urkel to it's sister TJ Max.  I've found some great deals here on all kinds of things.  If you're looking for inexpensive bedding in particular, this is where you want to be.  They also have some really strange housewares.  If you've ever wanted a three foot tall, green, ceramic owl, this is the Ross for you.
Came in with my family to shop...had loss prevention following me throughout the whole store. Very uncomfortable!!! Just got a set of earphones for my trip and left this shithole.
Talked to who I believe was a manager today named Yvette she was very rude and aloof on the telephone. I was planning on shopping there but I guess now I'll have to make another decision.

This is a fairly new Ross located in West Reno just off I-80.  I shopped here on a Monday around 1 PM and a Wednesday around noon.  On both occasions I found this store to be clean, neat, well organized and well stocked.  This is just what I like to see when I enter a Ross.  They had some nice, inexpensive designer purses, an excellent selection of comforters and other bedding, some high-quality towels and kitchenware, as well as some snowboarding items...both hard and soft gear.  They even had some inexpensive pet beds, both for fido and kitty.  When I return to visit my family in Reno, I will definitely shop at this Ross again.

We spent over 2 hours at this Ross one day. Their selection was larger than T J  Maxx's just down the way in the same mall area and their prices were very reasonable. There were a lot of good bargains to be had in the sale and clearance sections. Just come with a lot of time to comb through all the duds to find the gems. My friend found 20 items including tops, sweaters, skirts, pants, and dresses for about $300, that works out to $14.50 each. Not a bad deal when some items were over $50 originally. Also come with the patience that you only get 8 items to try in the dressing room at one time, needless to say, we went in there a few times. But go and good luck!

I enjoy this Ross and shop here quite often. It's usually clean, the workers are nice enough, and the clothes are at great prices and really cute. However I CANT stand the dressing room attendants. I'm not sure if they pick the newest workers to do that job or what... I get there is a certain limit on clothes, which is annoying and makes me not want to shop here, but the last time I walked up to the dressing rooms the attendant stared at my pile of clothes and exclaimed "wow that's a lot of stuff.... uh oh.." like yes that's what you do when you shop... you pick out lots of clothes and then you expect to try them on.. I always have to take 3+ trips to pick up my next set of clothes and the way they have it set up I have to leave all my clothes, both ones I liked and ones I didn't, outside the room just so I don't "steal" something... The thought of having to go there for clothes gives me anxiety but I love the stuff and the prices so I usually go back if I have a specific article of clothing in mind.. I never go just to browse anymore
Ross rock the shizzl on home good hidden treasures.  Hit or miss, I am addicted to snooping around the bargains

This Ross has a pretty nice selection of items compared to other Ross stores. I've looked before for yoga pants and only had 1 or 2 to choose from at other locations. I went to this one this Saturday and was happy to find several pairs to try on. I left with a great pair of shorts and pair of pants for yoga.  Everything else about it is typical Ross, busy, slightly disheveled, dirty dressing rooms. But if I can find what I'm looking for I'm a fan.

Wandering around this area, I discovered this store. Something about this chain of stores lately - it seems like there has been a lot less stock in the stores, lots of empty shelves.  And as I've thought a dozen times before, it's always off putting that the first thing you see when you walk into a store is a security guard eyeballing you.   Clothing quality seems to also have gone downhill.  As usual, look hard and you can find some bargains. For example, a little bed for my cat under $10. Some linens were nicely prices - queen sized coverlets under $40.

I'm really disappointed with this store. It's close to my house and I was excited for it to open, but despite multiple visits to the place, it has yet to meet my expectations.   It isn't well organized and is always understaffed. I have yet to find one of those steals that you expect from places like Ross, TJ Maxx, and Marshalls. The prices are very low, but the quality of clothes is pretty poor overall so you get what you pay for, I guess.  The home section is small and sloppy, but I did get cute curtain rods for only $12 a piece so not all is bad.  Worst of all is the customer service.  The store appears to be horribly understaffed.  They typically have one register open, even if there are 10 people in line.  Not great if you're in a hurry. It is also nearly impossible to find an employee on the floor if you need help with something.    Since it is nearby I'm sure I will continue to stop in occasionally, but the TJ Maxx at Lawrence Park is amazing and just slightly further away so it will remain my top spot for deal hunting.

I love me a good bargain, and Ross is always the one place I can count on for that rush!  This particular Ross is pretty well organized, they're open until 10:30 most nights, and some nights until 11, so that gives me plenty of time to shop!   However since I'm a compulsive shopper, that means I can't leave the place without spending at -least- $50. Tonight was no exception. 3 dresses, 2 shirts and several new panties later, and my wardrobe has a lovely spring flare!

I love the Ross Store much better than Kohls. I wish that we had a Ross Store here on Baltimore Pike. Between Clifton Heights PA and Springfield Pa.  If there can be so many Wawa Stores & CVS drug stores so close near each other  They can put Ross on the Pike. The only close one is in  Drexel Hill Pa .  They should take over were Burlington Coat factory has closed. Great Location.   I rate Ross a (10). Thank you  Pattie McGorman
The worst attention I've had from a cashier  she was talking with other coworker all the time and charged me 2 times a product

I found a dog bed and food/water bowls, a side table for my bedroom and a decorative bowl.  I may return for some living room tables.  They had great prices.  This location isn't too large but they had a good selection.  The cashier was very friendly and waited on my quickly.

When you go to a Ross, you have to expect that you'll need some time to search through all the racks and shelves to find the good stuff. This store is no different, except, like someone else said, half the racks seem empty so it takes much less time. As with many other Ross stores, the racks are in disarray and nothing is where it belongs. The women's clothing, which makes up the major portion of the store, is still lacking, and the kids and babies sections are practically nonexistant. Back in housewares, most of the items seem to have been opened and tampered with, and several things I purchased from there were missing parts once I got them home. This is also one of the messiest and most picked through Rosses I have ever been in.  They do get a star for their employees, who have always been nice, and for the fact that you can occasionally find stellar deals if you have the patience to look. I'll probably try a couple other Ross stores in Reno though before going back to this one again. Tl:dr- You may find something cheap and cool, but you'll probably also feel strangely depressed after a trip here.

My daughter and i stopped in on a whim as we were both needing a wardrobe update.   We had just shopped at a comparable nearby store where we had a good experience. What we found here were a large selection of summer clothes even though it was after July 4th. She walked away with 6 pair of shorts and 6 tops and a bathing suit for $160. Great price! All were current fashions which provided a nice update to her wardrobe. As for me: 2 beautiful new beach bags for $36 as well as a set of science fiction inspired coffee mugs for my man. This set was reasonably priced at $7.99 and he loves them.  With the lines moving fast on a Saturday because the checkers were both professional and customer oriented I know because of our pleasant experience we will return.

Great discount store.  But as most.. can't go there looking for a specific style/color.  I usually find my best bargains when I browsing for nothing in particular.  Love to go to their household aisles... always can find a decorating treasure hidden on the shelves waiting for you to take it home.

I do love Ross stores. I can find great deals on things that would usually cost me a fortune. Their quality of clothing for me has gone down a bit. I still manage to find some clothes I like. I did buy my winter coat there this year. Beats spending 150 for the same coat I seen someplace, I paid 45! I love their home section. They have tons of cool kitchen stuff and very nice frames all reasonable.

Management and employees are rude and don't follow store policies. Wouldn't let me return a shirt because the tags we're off even though it wasn't worn and I brought the tags and receipt. I had to call corporate to be able to do the return and the manager returned it as an MOS item which is not the case. The policy doesn't state anything about the tags being attached for shirts to return and the manager insisted she told the employees not to accept the items with detached tags. They don't follow the policies and this type of customer service will drive people away.

I am a fan of Ross stores, I have patronized these stores for a very long time. I recently have had some experiences at this stores that made my tastes change.   I have had a few problems buying products and having them fall apart within a couple weeks of purchases. I think that although they offer some decent products and good prices, one has to look into the quality and durability of the good/product. The return policy at this store makes it very hard to return a defective item.  Yesterday, I got a Starbucks coffee drink at Safeway and decided to get some clothes at this store. The loss prevention officer at the front of the store came charging at me as soon as I entered this store. She rudely started yelling at me that drinks are not allowed in this store and if I wanted to shop in there I would have to leave my drink up front or throw it away. I have shopped at very high end and low end stores and I have never encountered rude employees. Without saying anything I left the store and decided to take my purchases elsewhere.  I think that the employees at this store are very rude and make any shopping experience into a hostile experience. The loss prevention personal look like a bunch of ex-cons, they have no customer services skills.
Have to know how to shop.. When they receive new stock ..  Go great buys

This is one of the busiest Rosses I've ever been to. Having worked in this mall, I can say thats probably due to the location inside the mall. Its located near one of the entrances and the lines here can be horrifying (especially at holiday time). They do have speedy cashiers and most are usually very friendly. The store is kept pretty clean considering all the foot traffic this end of the mall gets.   There's the usual Ross crowd: screaming babies, children running around, teeny-boppers killing time before their parents pick them up, and people who have way too much in their carts to check out who end up slowing down the whole line. However, this is probably my favorite Ross store and having worked in one (in Goodyear), I know that keeping a store like this clean is damn near impossible. And so are some of the customers.   And its true, they do have some of the best deals and finds I've ever come across from a Ross. I've gotten several items here and have been happy with most. If I still lived in Tucson, I'd still probably be withering my paychecks by shopping here (ha!).

Ross usually has a great selection of clothing at a decent price. They used to have a BIG selection of plus sized clothing, but that has started to dwindle. I don't get it. If we make up more than 1/2 the market, why do we not get that much of the racks? Eh.. what ever.   I found what I was looking for and more, I ended up with 4 tops, a pair of shoes and some lingerie. I'm quite happy with my purchases.

I love this place!  I used to buy stuff from regular retails like Target and such but once I was introduced to Ross, I never buy home goods at regular prices.    For home goods like cookware, furniture, bathroom and bedroom products are usually organized and easy to look.  Clothing is a little bit more hassle because you have some digging to do.    I usually buy cookware for 50% off and I recently bought a Betsy Johnson watch for $22 and $1 Nike shorts and $32 DC shoes for my husband.    Sometimes there is a long line for checkout but it is all worth it!

It's a Ross. It's not the cleanest, it's not the most organized, but it has many of the things that I enjoy.  The hunt for bargains is part of the thrill when you go to a Ross. Sometimes You find some very good things, others you don't. It really is a toss up.  This one willfind me coming back to it on rare occasion though. If only to see what neat new things have arrived.

I just experienced some of the worst customer service. Apparently the general manager (Nichole) doesn't understand the concept of good professional customer service . I brought 2 items to return with receipt but missing the tags. I clearly showed her what items they were on the receipt yet she said she couldn't figure it out (again this is the general manager) she then said I need to go search the store to find the items so she could then figure out what they were. She was extremely rude and has zero customer service skills. I did go find the items and the girl in training was very helpful at least and credited back my return. Simple customer  service tip- be kind and helpful not a rude hateful person. It's not my fault you decided to work in retail.

Customer service is a low priority at this store. There are never enough cashiers  and the cashiers that I have experienced could care less about the customers. I have gone to this store since it opened and some things just never change.

AWFUL costumer service!!!! Called to ask about their return policy and nobody was able to answer. They left me on hold for like 5 minutes and still nobody answered my question. I hung up called again, and same thing happened. I was on the phone with them for about 30 minutes and when I asked to speak to a manager the lady said "we're kind of busy right now so can we call you later?" Mmmmmmm????!?! What?!? I just have a simple question about a product I got!!!!! UGHHH

The set-up was a bit awkward but I found some killer finds during my 10 minute visit including 3 BCBG sweater, 3 pairs of brand name sunglasses all under $10 an Adidas track jacket (a newer style) and much more... we stopped in because my gentleman friend forget his swim trunks on our mini vacay.

So this Ross is a proximity pick for me. Honestly, I prefer a TJ Maxx or Marshall's over a Ross any day.  In the case of this store, I'll usually end up there because of a subpar experience at the TJ Maxx in the next shopping center over.   This location is hit or miss, but typically has a large selection and definitely a large space than the aforementioned competitor.   Not my favorite, but totally good enough for some discount buys.

Security guard is nice, he/she will greet you when you enter the store.  But others staff are rude, unprofessional and not helpful. I was with my mom  continued two days shopping here. The fitting room ladies were rude. I greet them and tell them how many clothes we have. They instructed me (like a boss) to placed the clothes there and count. When we need to return few clothes, she don't even look at us until I asked her "can I place my clothes at the clothes Shelf"，then she rudely said " no no no, not there." Even though they were acting like this, mom and I still say "thank you " to them.  But this makes me feel disappointed and feel racism. We are same as customers here, is it because of we are Asian and you should be treated like us this way??? And somehow, I was 9 months pregnant. You don't care is fine but you are not helpful. The store is dirty and disorganized. It just near my house so we have no choice.

Even tho there was a very limited amount of jewelry, the quality is good and at a better price than what u would pay at Marshall's or TJMaxx.  The quality of clothes is subpar but you can sift through the selection of household things and find some good finds.
About what you would see in most overstock stores. Lots of fairly well disorganized selections, not terrifically clean, but if you know exactly what you're looking for bargains can be had!

This Ross has great bargains and stocked all the time.  The staff is not friendly at all.  Of all the Ross's in the area this has the least pleasant employees.  Pam is a employee there and she has a terrible disposition.

It takes along time to find a something but fun when u find something. You have to have a lot of time on your hands. I can spend five hours in the store searching for stuff. All the employees are so nice and sweet. They look like they are having fun at their job but are always very professional and treat customers with respect and just kindness.  Addicted shopper.
love the products they carry. best place to buy dresses, dishes,  pots and pans excellent prices on Linens.suh a great variery.
What a mess! The whole store is dirty and terribly unorganized! The staff isn't very warm and friendly either. I think goodwill is more organized than this place!

Mannnnn.... this place always has the deals. When it comes to home furniture, clothing, cosmetics, or jewelry, you can be sure to find a good deal here. My fine is a huge fan of this place. Even when we don't need anything, we find a great item that we could use in our home.
This is a great place to find some deals on name brand items without the name brand price. The staff is friendly, sometimes a little inefficient at check out but overall a good place to shop .
The staff is pretty 'meh' and everything always seems disorganized and strewn about. Just not really a fan of this location.

This Ross is the closest to my home in Seminole Heights. That said, it's not located in a particularly upscale area (being polite). There is an overall lack of organization and the inventory is pretty stale.  I have found some staples here (tights, home supplies, undies) but the shoe department is pitiful. The Fletcher Avenue location really is not a huge step up, but is certainly preferable over this one.

Nice for day to day stuff.  The only one we have visited is the one in Tampa.  Excellent household items and summer clothes.  Love their great prices and home decor.  You can get some good items for kids also.

'Loss Prevention' says the shirt the man at the entrance is wearing. I love that. It's a cute way of saying security without scaring the fragile suburbanites that travel onto the other side of city ave to peek inside Ross.  This place is usually a mess. More like a warehouse than a department store. Though once in a blue moon I will stop in and find something worth while.  I end up leaving every time wishing I wore size 13 shoes. My advice: TJMAXX is right down the block. Enjoy.

Plenty of parking the lot across the street at this ross.  I just say "OK" since I found a bunch of stuff that we could use in our home.    Prices are great!  Shelves were a bit bare.  As soon as you walk into the store you will find the shoe section which looks like need to be filled.  I wanted a swimsuit but only found one in my size.   I suppose it's July and it's busy but one would guess they should stock more especially being across the street from a swim club.   The cashier was very friendly.     Will I be back?  Sure if I am in the area but I doubt I will make a special trip.

A kids-free weekend meant my sister and I were able to shop and browse to our hearts delight...  Ross reminds me of a messier, less classy TJMaxx or Marshalls but I still like to shop here nonetheless.  This Ross was definitely messy, unorganized and quite busy but we found some great items for unbelievable prices! (Dress for $15, skirt for $7, dressy blouse for $8, Easter hand towels for $6)  This store was pretty crowded and the checkout line was looooooooonnnnnggggg.   I have to say, I hate how tight the rows of clothing and items are... like, it's quite difficult for 2 people to even pass by each other. You literally have to exit the row to let someone by (only to then NOT receive a "Thank you.")  Employees were friendly. I went into the fitting room like 4x and they didn't seem annoyed when I'd hand them a stack of clothes I didn't want. Cashier was nice and actually commented that she had been eyeing the skirt I bought.  I feel like you definitely need some time to browse because there are some good items here, you just have to search!

I have a love/hate relationship with Ross stores (mostly all of them). I love that you can find amazing deals and steals, but I hate how unorganized and cluttered their stores are, as well as how unenergized and slow their cashiers and employees are.   If you have the patience, then it may just pay off, as you can find some amazing prices, and this Ross location is just as great at finding great deals! You may have to dig a bit and search racks of unorganized and clothes thrown every which way, but you may just find exactly what you were looking for, saving a ton of money in the end. I have found great deals here, from under amour hoodies and north face shirts, to Nikes (free, air max, baseball cleats, etc), to name brand flip flops and packs of boxers/socks, all WAY below what they normally would be. I would say that some of these prices are even better than what you would find at an outlet store, but it's just a hit or miss. There's been times where I have visited the store, and spent $100 and walked out with a shopping cart full, and there's been other times where I've walked in and left a half hour later, having found nothing.   The thing that I dislike about most Ross stores, and this particular Ross is no exception, is that the stores are so cluttered. I don't know if it is because of the layout of the stores, the clientele, the lack of employee enthusiasm, or what. 99% of the time, there are clothes everywhere, lying on top of the clothing racks, lying on the floor, packages of t shirts and underwear opened and different pieces lying about, flip flops thrown every which way except how they are supposed to be, shoes all over the floor in front of the shoe racks, food items where the linens are and pillows and pool/bath towels left where the food and kitchen items are located. You just never know where you are going to find something. I've found amazing deals on an item tucked away somewhere. I clearance pair of Nikes stuffed behind some boxes of food goods, or a really nice under armpit polo stuck on a random rack nowhere near where it's supposed to be.  One other problem that unfortunately plagues any Ross store that I have ever been to is that the employees appear so carefree, lazy, and just all-around like they don't want to do their job, much less even be at work. There will be a line of 20 people waiting to checkout, with two cashiers (both working at an abhorrently slow pace), 10 other employees walking around, either appearing to do absolutely nothing, talking with another employee, or organizing something that could wait to be organized. I don't know if this problem is to blame on management, or even higher up in the company. If I only have one or two items in my hand, and there are a few people in line, then I will put those items back and leave, rather than stand there for a half hour in line. It's just not worth it sometimes. If you don't mind waiting in line and you've found a great deal, then it can definitely be worth the wait, just don't be surprised if the employees don't seem overly happy or energetic.

My family and I were on a family trip and we decided to stop by to pick up something we forgot to pack. We're waiting in line and I guess it turns out we were waiting in the wrong line, which was customer service, and the lady in the front named Claudia, told us we had to move to the other line for regular check-out. For once, there was no one else in either line besides us, after we moved we saw her whisper something to the customer she was helping. We patiently waited until someone else was willing to help, then the same lady "oh I can help whoever is next" and apparently she was talking to us, so she made us move for no reason and had the audacity to talk about us? My family and I, are Mexican and we didn't know why she was she was talking to us so rudely. I hope never to experience this again and we will certainly will not be returning.

An associate by the name of Brigette  works by the fitting rooms and is extremely rude. I went in today to try on some cloths, purchase a bed set and other items. When I went to try on my cloths I was not greeted nor was giving instructions on what their procedure was. Bri told me I needed to hang my cloths prior to entering the fitting room, I was unsure as to why because associates just usually ask how many items I have. When I asked her as to why she just repeated herself and started speaking to me as if I were a child - not even looking my way. I informed her that she did not need to speak to me that way. Bri continued along with rolling her eyes. Finally I hung all my cloths up like she asked and left. I was about to spend a little over $150 today and because of her poor service and attitude Ross lost my business. Especially this location.

I'm not the hugest fan of this Ross because it doesn't seem to get new inventory in very often, it's not in the best neighborhood, and the level of quality in their merchandise is questionable at times. However, I can't deny that I have walked away many times with amazing finds - you just have to have enough time to look long and hard through the store!

I experienced absolutely THE WORST customer service today by the "manager on duty". I found the perfect duffel bag for $16.99 as a Christmas gift for my son who's going to college. When I brought it up to the register the "manager on duty" wouldn't honor the ticketed price. Apparently one of her employees reticketed the item incorrectly, so she left me at the register while she looked for another bag, then came back and proceeded to cut off the ticket and attempt to charge me $27 (I believe, I was so appalled at this point that she wouldn't honor the ticketed price that I don't remember the exact number.)  When I pointed out that I had chosen the bag because of the price, and this this was a terrible customer service practice she offered me 10% off.   No way! It isn't my fault that someone employed by Ross under HER management made a mistake. She should have honored it and then had a meeting with her employees about it. Also, it wasn't a sticker price tag that could have been switched by a customer, the price ticket was attached to the item on a plastic ticketing ring.  I told her that I wanted to pay the price that was on the ticket and when she refused I pointed out that on MANY occasions Ross marks down certain items and won't mark down identical items that are a different color because the barcode is different. The other bag she brought up was a different color, so it is safe to assume that its barcode was different. She said there was nothing she could do. YES, she could have HONORED THE TICKETED PRICE.   I told her that this was terrible customer service and I wouldn't be returning to the store, and I absolutely mean it. Needless to say, I left without the ONE Christmas gift I knew my son would have loved.   I've shopped at Ross for over 20 years, and almost exclusively at this location since they opened. Apparently they need to brush up on their customer service practices and be more discerning as to who they hire as management.   The $10 you saved, dear Ross, cost you a loyal customer.   The Marshalls in the same plaza will get my business from now on. I'll gladly pay a little more if it means shopping from a company that doesn't humiliate and upset their customers over an employee mistake.

I consider Ross similar to a thrift store. I have to be in a certain mood to want to dig thru their overstuffed racks of clothing. I always come in here to look for summer dresses. No luck today but I did browse the home goods section and that was incredibly messy. The store always looks haphazardly put together. It would be easier to find the great stuff if everything was better organized.
Not located in the best area, a lot of times things are picked over or they hardly have new inventory. Loss prevention awkwardly stares as they have to be on alert for local thieves ...

When listening to music everything seems wonderful. Some people were glaring at me though....and you know what? There are not any specific area of the store with benches and mirrors to try shoes on. I kept getting told to get off the floor and sit all the way in the back where the metal table and chairs are. Those items are also on sale so it felt weird to sit on that chair. Meanwhile I have one shoe on and I am half hopping half walking to the other side while TRYING out shoes that are being sold at this store! They don't have a better system for this kind of merchandise?! People are a bit weird at this store. It seems like the comfort of others bothers them. If someone is daydreaming and wandering around harmlessly what business is it of you? If I am not hurting you in any physical way don't assume I'll hurt you at all! I really don't like negative vibes either but please don't think that daydreamers are evil undead creatures. God is an artist too and heaven may be a state of mind. I am working on myself constantly to think positive things. And I am on disability and poor myself! The cashier was very rude. Giving me a side glance and not wanting to look at me in the eyes then quickly saying thank you in a sarcastic tone to hurry me off to the side with a sideway glance. It wasn't just her eyes but the tone and infliction of her voice! At least she has a job!!

I will give an update that, this past weekend (perhaps for the holidays?) the staff seemed a lot more efficient and the line wasn't unbearable. They were moving people along and *gasp* there were 3 whole registers open. Not to mention the registers even looked like they were brand new! The powers that be must be paying attention to Yelp. Here is to hoping this Ross moves in the right direction in terms of better customer service and efficiency.

Okay...it's no Marshalls or TJ Maxx. But it is one of the better locations for Ross. Their merchandise isn't quite as disheveled as the Oracle location. The handbag selection is better here as well. They do seem understaffed, especially on the weekends. But I still receive relatively good customer service. Nothing above and beyond, but they are polite and friendly.

Worst experience I've ever had by far shopping.  Waited in line for a good 10 minutes and was the next person to be helped a couple walked in to the store and got into the return line about 8 minutes into me standing in line.  Meanwhile a woman's screaming child whom she gave no fucks about carried on and the other couple behind me in line argued.  Already on edge because of all the commotion and the wait the clerk kid sees me standing there for 10 minutes and calls the return customers over who've been waiting maybe a minute or 2.  I stormed over to the fitting rooms and asked for a manager.  What I got was a laughable manager on duty.  I explained to her how the kid just skipped over me and she pretended to apologize and act like I was being irrational in complaining.  So after she finally goes to help the kid get through an enormous line she proceeds to make me wait very last in line. So after another 10 minute wait I'm boiling over.  I ask to speak with her manager and she tells me that she's it.  Not only is the store being run by what I assume is an over glorified clerk (having worked in retail and knowing what manager on duty means), but they don't even have an actual manager there to over see how shitty they're being run?  After I talked to her she about how I was frustrated that she proceeded to make me wait seeing as I just complained to her about being skipped over and not even given a thought, she acted like "oh well what are you going to do".  I have never wanted someone to be a man so that I can knock their block off in my life.  I will never go to that shit hole again.

This store has great prices and more name brands then most of the other ross stores. I love the jessica simpson shoes they have allways.If you know about those they are $100 dollars or more .Not at ross $ 20 .Great deal They have brands like bcbg, hurley, tilt, and so many more name brands. If you like ross try this one it rocks !!!

I only go here out of necessity; times when I need to grab something quick and know I can find it for cheap. Generally, I prefer the TJ Maxx up the way.  What I don't get is how there almost always is a long line. Don't let someone in front of you be buying multiple items, you'll be there a while. Like half the registers look like they're collecting dust. Today my cashier was nice, but I'm almost certain he's the same guy who does security. Are they that short-staffed? Meanwhile, an actual Ross cashier, his co-worker, stood at a cash register without opening up a line.  Just stood there chatting with the nearby cashiers. I'm seriously wondering if their cash registers simply don't work here. They're apparently just for show.   One time I went and some random kid was just playing around at an empty (probably defunct) register, but the staff didn't even say anything.   One pro: I had no problems with the staff today, probably because it was the security guy.

This Ross is pretty good. The other Ross's in the area consist if Zephyrhills and Land O Lakes.  This time around there was barely any clearance racks. That was sad. Where did they all go?  I like shopping in their shoes, clothes, home, and doggie stuff. So many interesting finds here.  They also keep up on their holiday decor which is quite cute.

This Ross kinda sucks. Though I did find a dress for my night out, I couldn't find any shoes. Every shoe was either a flat or stripper heel. They barely had any shoes in size 9. WTH?   And the kids clothing area is SO scarce! They really need to restock.   Not good for first impressions!

The thing about Ross is that you have to know what brands found in Ross are the best. Some brands fall apart quickly, while others seem to last a long time. If you know which brands are the best, you will love shopping at Ross. The prices are great, and the store is always clean. The customer service is not exceptional, but is far better than a lot of other stores in the Reno area. My favorite thing I ever found at Ross was a pair of Lucky Brand Jeans - for $12.

I tried and tried and tried again but I can never find anything in this place..NOTHING!  I know it's fairly new BUT but now they should of have those shelfs stocked. There is no customer service, only person who ever speaks is security (loss prevention) and I'm not sure if he does that so your aware he is there or he is just being friendly..If your looking for some major deals I would look at a different location.

It always pays to look here because the selection changes. I've found some good bargains in kitchen utensils, housewares, and decorative items.  This particular location is much less crowded than those in large cities. The staff is courteous and helpful, and the wait time at the checkout is short.

Since this is the only Ross near my house I had no other choice to go to this location. I try to avoid going in there because of bad customer service and they barely have anything stocked. I wanted to buy some pants and ended up finding a dress and shoes. At checkout the girl was about to put my dress and shoes in the same bag and when I politely asked her to put my shoes in a separate bag she stoped what she was doing and looked at me like I asked for the most difficult thing in the world. Not sure if she doesn't have common sense not to put shoes people have tried on already and been on the floor in the same bag as clothes. Needles to say the associates there are terrible and they really need to get a whole new staff. Will never be going back and rather spend the extra time to travel to another Ross

Just left and was nearly shoved out of the way for the next customer.  I understand they need efficiency but to shout out instructions to customers to assist the cashier then call the next customer before you've been handed your receipt is just tacky.  Nothing is in any sensible order either.  If you're looking for a ross with nice selection, good atmosphere and thought out product placement this is not the one.  I almost feel apologetic to the employees for shopping there. Definitely felt like i was a nuisance.

This Ross is relatively clean, but can get pretty packed during the weekend.  They do not have a great selection of clothes, but again everything here is cheap so that makes up for it.  Definitely one of the nicer Ross' in Tucson.

If you have time and want great products for cheap this is the place to go. You can't beat the quality of products for the price. Normally I have ok customer service, and the security guy always greets me, but I'm a pretty independent shopper so as long as you're not insanely rude I don't mind. However the past few times I've been in the store I've received exceptionally mediocre to poor customer service. I was going to try on a pair of pants and literally watched to workers sit 3 feet away from where I stood (the only person waiting for a room number) and they didn't even acknowledge my existence. I get it; they probably have to deal with crummy customers making demands all day, I don't mind if you can't help me, just give a girl a holler saying it'll be a minute! Maybe the employees are disgruntled because they aren't paid well or something? Idk, give those ladies a raise or something bc it was like jumping thru hoops just to get out of that store. While I never did end up trying on those pants, I will certainly be back because like I said, good products at even better prices, plus it's not too disorganized so you can browse with a fairly aesthetically pleasing experience.

Anne H. is apparently way more knowledgeable about Ross's brands than I am, but I know enough to shop here.   I've purchased clothing, art, bedding, gifts and housewares at this store.   The Prices are great! The customer service is not! Return policies are horrid. Return lines can be sooooooo slooooooow!   Nevertheless, if you are a bargain hunter in Reno, and shopping for new as opposed to used goods, Ross will show up on the list of your top four places to check along with Marshalls, Tuesday Morning, and TJ Max.   Since I HATE TO SHOP, my shopping trips are generally one store affairs. If I go into a store I'm pretty certain I'm going to find what I want or need -- or something I didn't know I needed.   Without fail, I find one of the three each time I visit Ross. The problem is that I don't really enjoy the atmosphere or employee attitudes.
This is a very clean store and well organized.  The staff keep the merchandise well stocked and your can find some REAL nice deals here.

This is a perfect example of see something, say something! Do not shop here! Especially if you're a woman shopping alone. I have never actually feared for my safety while shopping before today.  There is a extremely overly aggressive theft prevention employee that works there.  I went into this store to simply exchange a rug for another color that I had purchased for my daughter.  I did not have my receipt, which I didn't think much of since I used my credit card and the tags were still attached.  The the cashier was completely ok with this as well (As I would think should be) but the guy in the black vest, not so much.  He actually stopped me and said "you don't have a receipt?!" So strongly that I thought he must be joking. He wasn't.   I did some additional shopping, all the while keeping an eye out for that man in the black vest that made me so uncomfortable. I went to make my purchase and exchange and guess who was there..one of the most aggressive and rude people I've ever come in contact with while shopping.  He stood at the counter next to me while I completed my transaction. He started making comments"What is that smell?!"  "Oh it's that rug you brought in!"  I said " oh no, do you guys not keep your merchandise clean?"  Bc that rug has been in my bmw in a bag for a few days. He continued to make comments about myself, the rug, etc in front of several customers.  I asked to speak to a manager, which may have only been the 3rd time doing in my entire life.  He stood at the counter making non stop eye contact with me. I told him to please join our conversation if he had something to contribute as he was again making me extremely uncomfortable.   He mouthed off in front of the manger who shook his head and told him to stop.  He then called me ridiculous and walked away. As I was getting my items out of the cart, he stared at me the entire time.   As I walked to my car, still in disbelief of the situation, I warned a woman walking in who actually shared a very similar story!  Why is he working here?  It takes a lot to frighten me. I will never enter this store again, and I hope no one else does as well until he is fired.

There is a reason they have the slogan 'Dress for less.'  The quality of clothes at this place is crappy, no bones about it. I've never found 'designer' clothing either. On an occasion or two I've found a great pair of yoga pants or a work out shirt, but that is the extent of the clothing. They do have branded children's clothes at decent prices. You have to be careful though because I've spotted holes in the clothing where the security tag is. Now if you want a deal on a bath mat, towels, or kitchen utensils, you  may be in business. The store is very clean. However, who wants to walk into the store and be greeted by a 'mall cop.'  It makes me feel uncomfortable....."I'm watching you....bwah ha ha!'

Well, it's a Ross. Cheap designer clothes. The problem with offering these clothes for such low prices is that you attract a lot of less-than-savory individuals. Other than that, it's a great deal and you'll find all kinds of useful things in there. Just make sure you wash them before you wear them.

I really teetered between 2 and 3 stars on this one so I took out a handy piece of paper and started with 5 stars.  From that point I went through the experiences I had and either added or subtracted a star until I came to the end of the trip and it totaled to 3 so 3 it is.  I might prefer to say 2.5.  I wondered into this store with my daughter because I had 1 1/2 hours to kill and I was trying to find stuff to spend money on.  We walked around the entire store and ended up filing our basket with random stuff we didn't really need but decided we wanted.  Included in the basket were two pairs of Guess shoes, a dress for me, a huge piece of canvas artwork, hair stuff for my daughter, a lap top pillow, a journal and some other things.  The store is like any other Ross - sort of clean and sort of not.  A tad disorganized but nothing that screamed "thrift store".  Reason #1 that they lost a star (and this has already been mentioned) is that I caught the Loss Prevention guy following me around.  Not only was I insulted that he thought I was going to steal something (come on dude - am I going to shove this canvas artwork that's taller than I am in my purse and make a run for it?) but he was kinda creeping me out.  I started walking around faster to try to lose him.   Reason #2 that they lost a star:  I went into the dressing room to try on a dress which ended up look super awesome.  I went out to my waiting cart and asked if I could take the shoes in to see what they look like with the dress in the full length mirror.  I was told no by Tatiana ( I think that's her name and how to spell it ).  She was not very nice about it and when I told her that I didnt understand why I can't take them in another 10 steps to see she rolled her eyes and walked away.  Wow.  After Tatiana crossed the eye rolling line my daughter and I put 99% of the impluse purchases back.  I ended up buying the dress and hair ties.  We spent a whopping $30.00 instead of the $150.00 we had in the cart.    I can't deduct anymore stars because the place was not dirty or baron.  I might go back or I might go somehwere else - just not sure.   I could have overlooked the security dude and given it a 4 star raiting but Tatiana really bummed me out.

Nice store. Last time I was in here the loss prevention kid had no idea what to do except follow around attractive women and stare. Store has a lot of merchandise that it keeps well rotated. Staff is helpful which is a nice change from other locations in the area.

Store was very disorganized with items on the aisle floor. Home decor section shelves were bare.  Directional signs on the floors were beginning to come up which left dirty, sticky spots on the floor.  Shelf signs were posted asking shoppers for patience while they restocked.  I have to wonder how long customers were needing to wait? I will try back later this year.  Maybe then this Ross will be back to the high standard I had become accustomed to.
This place is clean. Its pretty well organized as well. I wish there was more childrens clothing thou.

I love Ross stores, but some locations are a bit disorganized and have rude employees.This location is always well-organized and the employees are always really nice. Tonight we were helped by Sandy in the dressing room and again at the cash register. She and I chatted while my son tried on clothes and I watched her as she helped other shoppers. She was friendly, even after some of them were a bit discourteous, greeting each one with a smile. Great customer service!

This Ross is clean and organized, however the cashier is always missing and has an attitude when she notices someone is waiting for her. She is an older woman with short dark hair. Not very pleasant. They have a great selection of well EVERYTHING of course. Customer service is a little on the iffy side especially back in the fitting room area.. u bring one item up hold it up tell them it's one item and they still wanna hang it and count it themselves. This Ross tends to be very busy when I am in there and honestly this fitting room "Clothes gotta be hung here So we can count them" deal has made customers just throw their items to try on - on he nearest rack from where they are standing and leave and head next door to Marshall's because doing this causes a line when u can just simply state the # of items u have. Yes I understand it's an LP thing but your losing customers and also the fitting rooms are way too hot . U sweat your ass off in there makes u not wanna even try things on. Keep the fitting rooms nice and airy so customers will want to try things on and make purchases instead of getting agitated dealing with the tedious fitting room attendant and finally the annoyed cashier that I guess forgot what her job consisted off.

It's a love hate relationship with Ross. If a store is located in a nice area you definitely can find some good deals and steals. On the flip side, if located in a lower income area, things are definitely picked through. Not saying you still won't find good deals but maybe the options are not as plentiful. I didn't get a chance to go through the whole store at this location but I was able to pick up some gardening tools for 1/2 or 1/3 of the price at other stores. I also had some really good finds on planters for my indoor plants that I really like for close to nothing! Super excited to use my gardening tools and repot my plants.   I also found some tea tree 100% Dead Sea bath salts as well as cleansing charcoal bath salts. Excited and really curious on using these!  Ross is convenient to stop by when you're in a rush and need to find something that will quickly hold you over. Or if you're in a budget and need to pick up a quick gift for someone. One stop shop!  Now I have to go to another Ross to find other unique planters and Knick knacks hahaha

Dont come here anytime soon.  Ladies if you're wanting to try something on you can't.     Fitting rooms are closed.    I had a basket full of garments to try on and no fitting room. I'm now on a nationwide search to find pants since Sears closed down. So far been to Walmart, Old Navy, and even Goodwill to no avail. Terrible customer service, the lady running the fitting rooms was extremely rude and made multiple sarcastic comments, out of jealousy I guess. It was the worker with the British accent, the other staff workers seemed nice. Experience ruined by one worker.

This location is kind of a disaster. Never fails to be a total mess and have a super long checkout line. Noon on a Saturday before Christmas and only one cashier?!  Oh wait, they have two, but one of them is not at her register. ROSS sucks!  When my wife and I go there, they never have the cool stuff they show on the commercials!!  And, the workers are rude and snooty!!!

This ROSS was very neat and organized. I travel to alot of different Ross's and this was one of the neatest Ross's. All of the aisles were neat and tidy down to cashier lane.   As I entered the store the Loss Prevention security guard greeted me with a smile as I entered and exited the store. The lady working the area near the fitting rooms was alright I suppose. My cashier "ALexis" was great, she smiled and thanked me for my business.   If I had to name something I disliked about this store it would be that Alexis was the only cashier and the line was long. It wasn't Alexis's fought at all-but that's the only thing I didn't like was that there was only one cashier station were available for use.   Great Ross store though, I shall return!
I love this store they always have good prices and great products.. the staff is always friendly and helpful.. there are tons of clothing items to choose from and new stuff all the time..

Ross is my next favorite for getting glam on a budget. Marshalls, TJ Maxx, and Marshalls are all owned by the same parent company, but they are all VERY different and require different strategies. For whatever reason, this is my favorite Ross in Reno- I'm convinced it's because of this neighborhood's suburban demographics, fellow shoppers are not looking for the same stuff I am, so I WIN! Checkouts are pretty smooth and they have more people here now, avoiding the snaking check-out lines that can plague Ross stores. This store is always super neat and tidy, too.  Rules of Ross: 98% of the stuff here is just HORRIBLE. Vile fabrics, awful cuts, things that someone dumped out of a semi and drove off. Avoid, avoid! 2% of the stuff is GREAT. I have hit Calvin Klein gold mines here- beautiful sleeveless blouses, sleek layering pieces, work-appropriate separates. For about 50-70% off retail. I've also noted their workout clothes can have some hidden gems- yoga tops and the like for good prices. You can also find some beautiful Polo/Ralph Lauren shirts for men ($14.99!!). The key to find the great stuff is to drop by and do a quick scan at the front and do a fabric/brand check, going down the aisles and spending about ten minutes to screen. I have dropped by the store more than a few times and left empty-handed, but keep your sleuthing skills up and you will be rewarded. A fun modern-day treasure hunt!

I was sooo HAPPY that I had a Ross 4 minutes from house been new to the area, but this is the WORST ROSS when you get to the cashiers.... They shoved everything on the bag. They don't even take the time to fold your clothes (a simple 3 steps) I thought it was my cashier but it's alllllll of them.... I'll be making my 30 minutes drive to the one at Brandon....

I will literally NEVER shop at the Ross Dress for Less (Wesley Chapel, FL) again! Looking for a place where the cashiers can easily steal from you? This is it!  The way their counters are set up allow for them to steal your items. I like this Ross. Lots more selection then the nearby Grove Wesley Chapel location. It's nice and clean and organized. The service is nice. Manager is helpful. This is a one stop shop plaza. Ross, Marshalls, Bealls Outlet all in one place. You don't need to leave. Just shop!!
Ghetto ghetto ghetto!!!!!!!!! The staff is rude. Avoid this place at all cost!! Place was dirty, felt like I was at a flea market

Have closed the back dressing rooms, the front two rooms are so small you cannot turn around. have one cashier and in line for almost 39 minutes on a Saturday morning.  Have experienced this before. So sad, it is a great store. Staffing very poor.

Let me just start by saying I LOVE Ross but there is a  associate who doesn't were a name tag at this location who is SUPER GHETTO.  I had to bring back a area rug they forgot to take the security sensor off.   The person was super rude, unprofessional and combative. My trip to this Ross was okay it wasn't anything special I found a nice top that I like and I bought that I looked at some of their perfumes and I didn't find anything that suited my interest but they do have a large selection of women's clothing most of it is pretty cheap but you can find some nice stuff in quality manufacturers mixed in with the more generic playing manufacturers with the more plain clothing. There seems to be more security workers work in the aisles than there are helpers and that is an indicator to me that I may not want it too much more shopping at the store since there's so much loss prevention folks all over the place. Luckily I found the top I like and I hope it lasts for a while because it fits perfect! I would say that if you're going to come to this Ross to come during the weekday because on the weekends I've been here and it's super busy even today on a Thursday the line was 4 people.

Managers and associates are very friendly in wesley chapel, Florida  location . I used to work for ROSS in California and I just recently moved to Florida. Florida people are wayyyyyyyyyy nicer than California people.  The store was very clean and they are extra friendly. Their shipment is way nicer than California. I applied for this location and I hope I get it soon
Christmas time 42 people in line only 2 cashiers open. For a big box store very poor management.

I almost always find what I am looking for at Ross and for reasonable prices. Today we went to get shoes for the kid (17) and they had just what he needed and in his size! This store does not feel too crowded like some discount stores and they always have new items at the front to look through.
Great staff, they work very hard and do very well dealing with fluctuating merchandise and rude, entitled customers.
Crap crap and more crap selection.   We wound up buying hair bands and some chocolates.   I will say that it was clean and well organized .

Perhaps if they could afford to hire more workers, more people might shop here.  15 people in line to make purchases with 1 cashier and no one available for returns clearly shows the MOD is probably focused on keep his/her labor hours low for a bonus than taking care of customers.    I wonder why every time. I shop in this store or actually any other Ross, they NEVER have enough cashiers on duty for the volume of business they have. This place I soooooo rundown!!! There are terrible unprofessional associates working here. This Ross needs to retrain all their employees! Why? We decided to come here on a Thursday night to see if we can find some foam mats for a bargain deal. We were able to find some but it was cheaper than other places by 2$ so not a huge discount.
